forks.overview: A renamed, actively maintained fork (68 merged PRs between 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-14) that publishes itself on npm as `droidsembly` (0.4.0-beta.x on the `next` tag). It is becoming a bilingual (English/Italian) product built around OpenCode V2: the CEO and workers can run on OpenCode V2 models, it tracks AI usage across Claude, Codex and OpenCode with a quota gate per resource, it adds a read-only analysis task and manager refinements after QA, and it swaps the people for robots with a cyan rebrand. It forks from exactly upstream 157efde (behind 0). dev is 171 commits ahead (509 files, +19.8k/-3.1k), and about a third of those commits are validation/evidence docs. main holds only merge commits on top of dev, and its tree is 8 commits behind dev.
forks.license_note: LICENSE is unchanged (MIT), and package.json still has license MIT and author Leon van Zyl. The fork adds bundled third-party license notices (scripts/licenses/*, dist/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt) and ships the Sora font under the OFL (client/public/icons/Sora-OFL.txt). The package name and bin changed to droidsembly, and the issue templates point to droidsembly.com. No telemetry was added: the only new outbound fetches are the npm registry update check and OpenCode/ElevenLabs calls that already existed.

features.title: Multi-provider AI usage telemetry and per-resource quota gating
features.description: Records token and cost observations for each assistant message (input, output, reasoning, cache read/write, costUsd) from Claude (SDK messages and statusline), Codex (an allowlisted transcript reader inside the Codex hook, capped at 16 MB) and OpenCode V2 (a plugin hook). Each observation is tagged by agent, repo, tool, provider and model. It replaces the office-wide Claude pacing/pause with a QuotaGate per resource, keyed by a hashed tool+provider+account+access, so hitting one provider's limit holds only the work on that quota. The manager can group resources into a shared quota, resume pacing per resource, and see an AI usage panel (resource rows plus the latest 200 observations). New REST routes: /api/usage/resume, /api/usage/group, /api/usage/simulate.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream 157efde only has a global, Claude-only pause/pacing (server/swarm.ts:3795 `private pausedUntil = 0`, `private limited()` at 3875, server/pacing.ts). It has no per-provider token or cost observations and no Codex/OpenCode usage. All fork commits are dated after upstream main, and upstream main is the merge base.
features.rationale: This is the closest existing piece to the factory's cost/model-routing layer: per-model token and cost data plus resource-scoped quota gates are the base for budgets and routing decisions. Do not cherry-pick it. It rewrites swarm.ts pacing (~280 lines changed), its OpenCode half depends on the V2 plugin, and `state.aiUsage` grows without bound inside state.json (mergeUsage scans the whole array with findIndex on every insert; only the view is sliced to 200). Port shared/aiUsage.ts, server/quotaGate.ts and the Claude/Codex adapters. Keep observations in a bounded or rotated store, not state.json, and add a fake usage stream to demo.ts, which emits none today.
features.risks: The Codex hook reads the session transcript file (allowlisted fields, 16 MB cap). The OpenCode plugin reads the active credential's connection id, which is hashed before it is stored. Behavior changes: the global usage pause becomes per-resource, and 'Resume full speed' now needs a chosen resource. state.json grows without limit.

features.title: Manager 'Request changes' on a PR that already passed QA
features.description: Adds a 'Request changes' button on Kanban for PRs whose QA passed. The manager must write a note. The PR goes back to the fix queue with fixReason 'manager' and a requestedSha. The old QA report and passedSha are kept, but a new QA round is required before merge. The QA retest prompt says the earlier pass was not a failure and checks the manager's request against the diff since the last review. fixOutcome, catchUp and restart recovery all treat a pending manager request as unsatisfied.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/sendBack.ts:54 accepts only 'needs-human' or 'failed' records, so a PR that passed QA cannot be sent back, and upstream has no 'manager' fixReason.
features.rfc_relation: approvals, human review gate, QA loop
features.rationale: A small, well-tested human-in-the-loop gate that fits the planned 'human approval -> build -> QA -> merge' flow. The server part of 4ac28f4 applies cleanly to upstream main (checked with git apply --check). The client part (KanbanView, qaCard, AppViewer) uses the fork's t() i18n helper and needs plain strings, or the i18n port.
features.risks: Starts a paid agent session, which the dialog warns about. No external services.

features.title: Read-only 'analysis' task for an agent (no issue, worktree or PR)
features.description: New agent task type 'analysis' (POST /api/agents/:id/analyze, 1-4000 characters). The agent's CLI runs in the floor's main checkout with a prompt-level read-only contract (no edits, shell, commits, issues or PRs), and follow-up messages are allowed. The restart does not resume it, it is refused for the CEO and for cloud agents, and a missing checkout fails it without preparing a desk. The final reply is shown as safe Markdown in the terminal view, with the raw terminal collapsed. The demo has a fake.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no 'analysis' task. Every agent task goes through issue -> desk -> PR in server/swarm.ts.
features.rationale: It is a working template for a non-PR, artifact-producing agent step, which the plan -> spec -> independent review stages need. Port it as a general 'artifact task' (plan, spec, review) that saves its Markdown output as a first-class artifact instead of reading it back out of the terminal log. 232931d does not apply cleanly (swarm.ts drift, i18n), and the analysis code is woven into the OpenCode V2 commit 8adf85b, so lift it by hand.
features.risks: Read-only is enforced only by the prompt, which matches cubefarm's 'no sandboxes' rule but means the CLI keeps full access.

features.title: Opt out of CEO onboarding and auto-merge when connecting a project
features.description: floorOptions gains onboardCeo (default true) and autoMerge (default true) for connect, create and publish in the ProjectPicker. Setting onboardCeo to false skips the CEO's onboard/plan jobs, and setting autoMerge to false creates the floor with manual merge from the start.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream connectRepo hard-codes `autoMerge: true` and always enqueues the CEO onboard job.
features.rationale: A cheap governance default. A factory that wants human approval before merging should let a project start with auto-merge off. It sits inside commit 8adf85b, so re-implement the ~30 lines rather than cherry-pick.
features.risks: None.

features.title: OpenCode V2 runtime for workers and the CEO, with a model/variant catalog picker
features.description: Rewrites the OpenCode integration for OpenCode 2.x: a V2 plugin object, --standalone sessions with a deterministic session id, a dedicated 'cubefarm' primary agent so the model#variant choice sticks, model switching on resume, a remote MCP office server, and the V2 providers config for local models. A version gate refuses OpenCode 1.x. Lets the CEO run on OpenCode (office_ tool prefix in the CEO prompt) and resets the CEO's session and model when its CLI changes. Adds GET /api/opencode/models with a cached, sanitized catalog (providers, variants, tools capability) and an OpenCodeModelPicker UI. Keeps OpenCode's final reply in the scrollback after a full-screen exit. Also handles the Windows desktop app's %LOCALAPPDATA% .exe shim.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream supports OpenCode 1.x for workers only: server/clis.ts uses `provider`/`npm: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, `--model`, and a 1.x plugin, while server/swarm.ts:2682 forces the CEO to `'claude'`. Upstream #311 (local models for OpenCode) uses the 1.x config this fork replaces.
features.rationale: Two ideas are worth taking: letting the CEO run on a non-Claude CLI, and a live model catalog with variants for routing. The catch is that the fork drops OpenCode 1.x completely and rewrites the opencodeLocal config that upstream #311 just added. Import it only behind version detection (keep 1.x working), and lift the catalog/picker and the CEO-CLI choice separately. The cmd-shim fix is a small standalone win.
features.risks: Breaking for OpenCode 1.x users. It depends on an external CLI's V2 API (`opencode api get /api/model`), which is still moving. It changes the local-model provider config format.

features.title: Office language setting (English/Italian) for the UI, CEO replies and speech
features.description: An office-wide `settings.language` ('en'|'it'). A dictionary with English strings as keys (shared/i18n.ts plus italianUi/Operations/Navigation/Specialized/PhoneAccess, about 1000 strings), with `translate()`, a `useT()` hook and a `<T>` component, plus a coverage test. Translates nearly every overlay: the manager console, Kanban, mission control, time-lapse, HUD, help, photo mode, games, careers and pocket mode. communicationInstructions() makes the CEO and analysis agents reply in the office language, ElevenLabs and browser speech get language codes, and the browser voice is picked by language. Code, issues and PRs stay in English.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no i18n module. Its shared/ has no i18n.ts, and UI strings are hard-coded English.
features.rationale: Useful to a Hungarian-speaking owner as a framework: copy shared/i18n.ts, client/src/i18n.tsx, LanguageSelect and communicationInstructions, widen Language to include 'hu', and move strings over one file at a time. Do not cherry-pick the 89-file UI churn (+3000/-1750 in client/src/ui alone), because every upstream UI change would then conflict. English-text keys are simple, but every copy edit silently drops the translation (the coverage test only partly guards this).
features.risks: Large merge-conflict surface. The language instruction is added to every CEO message and analysis prompt, which costs a few tokens per session.

features.title: Dictation startup feedback and speech-recognition error handling fixes
features.description: A startup timeout now reports an actionable error instead of cancelling silently. A recognition error fails the session at once (some browsers never fire onend after an error). abort() detaches all handlers so late events cannot revive or deliver a stopped session. A 'starting' state is distinct from 'listening'. Recognition uses the office language instead of navigator.language.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream client/src/ui/mic.ts still calls cancel('stopped') on startup timeout and only fails in onend.
features.rationale: These are real browser bug fixes in voice input, but they are tangled up with translate() inside the i18n commit. Re-apply the mic.ts logic changes and the micStartup tests without the i18n plumbing.
features.risks: None.

features.title: Serialized terminal saves, idempotent shutdown, journal stop, awaited preview cleanup
features.description: AgentTerminal.save is serialized, so overlapping saves no longer race on the same .tmp file and rename (an EPERM risk on Windows). Swarm.shutdown() is idempotent, blocks new save timers once stopping, and always writes the final state. Terminal saves run in parallel with a bound of 8 and no overlapping periodic batches. Journal.close() stops writers that were still awaiting the filesystem. Preview idle cleanup resolves only after the app/worktree teardown. notifier.notify returns a promise for its immediate deliveries. Adds a Windows Node 22 CI job.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/terminal.ts save() writes `${file}.tmp` with no serialization, and upstream Swarm.shutdown is a plain async function that can run twice. 5e15a87 and c1ee377 apply cleanly to upstream main (git apply --check).
features.rationale: Root-cause fixes to upstream code paths that the live office runs on Windows. 5e15a87 (without docs) and c1ee377 apply cleanly. The swarm.ts half of 5cbfcca needs 5e15a87 first, and its previews/vitest parts apply on their own. Skip the CI matrix additions unless wanted.
features.risks: None external. Changes shutdown ordering, so retest office restart in demo mode.

features.title: Dependency installs own their timeout; npm ci progress lines
features.description: The preparing-desk watchdog no longer flags a desk as stuck while npm ci is queued or running under its own 15-minute timeout (`dependenciesPending`). While the install is quiet, it writes 'npm ci is still running (N min elapsed)' every minute, and setup notes also go to the agent's live terminal.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/watchdog.ts flags any 'preparing' agent after PREPARING_MS no matter whether an install is running, and upstream deps.ts has no progress interval.
features.rationale: A small fix for false 'stuck' alarms on large repos. The deps.ts and swarm.ts parts apply cleanly. watchdog.ts has a one-hunk conflict because the fork edited it earlier, which is trivial to resolve.
features.risks: None.

features.title: Bound the CEO MCP endpoint's input size and nesting; patched body-parser/qs, SDK and zod minimums
features.description: /api/mcp/:token now has a 1 MB body limit (was 4 MB). Before any MCP server or zod validation runs, an iterative walk rejects bodies with more than 10,000 elements or nesting deeper than 64 (returns 413). The handler moves to server/mcpHttp.ts. Raises @modelcontextprotocol/sdk to ^1.32.2 and zod to ^4.6.7, and updates body-parser to 2.4 and qs to 6.17 with offline regression tests.

features.title: Patched production and dev transitive advisories with offline lockfile tests
features.description: Lockfile bumps for hono, @hono/node-server, fast-uri, ip-address (production) and vite 8.3.5, vitest 5.0.3, concurrently (dev), plus tests that assert the patched versions in package-lock.json.

features.title: Cloud Box: verified exit status, and desk preparation scoped to a subshell

features.title: Cloud cost controls: verified Box removal, 'pause new cloud work' switch, onboarding guidance

forks.overview: A heavily diverged, very active personal fork (last push 2026-11-14, 190 PRs of which 186 merged, mostly written by its own office agents and Codex). It forked at upstream Release 0.3.2 (11237cf, 2026-10-01), never merged upstream back (135 commits behind, including upstream's role removal #288, cloud agents #309, outbox patches, presence and all the 3D fun features) and is 213 commits / ~59k added lines ahead across 487 files. It has turned cubefarm into a governance-heavy software factory: Idea -> PRD -> two independent reviews -> manager approval -> held cross-floor issue publication, prototypes, researchers, QA/security review pipeline with release-shipped skills and playbooks, merge queue, run history / scores / lessons telemetry, an SSH worker fleet, Upstash workers, a manager MCP gateway, Telegram and a 2D dashboard. It still uses explicit roles (dev, qa, researcher, ceo), so almost everything needs adapting before it fits upstream's interchangeable agents.

The new skills/ directory vendors third-party agent skills, each with its own MIT LICENSE kept in place (Matt Pocock, Anthropic, Cloudflare, Jesse Vincent/obra, Siqi Chen, DietrichGebert, jovd83, Eric Tech), with pinned upstream revisions listed in skills/README.md. package.json adds @upstash/box, playwright 1.64.1 and yaml as dependencies, and ships docs/specialisms and skills in the npm package.

features.title: Ideas workflow: Idea -> researched PRD -> two independent reviews (max 3 rounds) -> manager approval card -> held, verified cross-floor issue publication
features.description: The manager submits an Idea (description, links, constraints, floor hints) from the console or MCP. A lead researcher session returns a zod-validated report: a clarifying question, requests for focused evidence from floor researchers (max 12), or a PRD (problem, outcome, scope, linked evidence, assumptions, target floors with rationale, measurable acceptance criteria). The lead drafts a revisioned Issue Plan: one-session issues per configured floor with requirement IDs (R1..Rn), optional Tracking Parents, a dependency graph checked for cycles, and reuse of or overlap with existing open issues. Two agents other than the author review the exact PRD+plan revision, one for evidence/requirements and one for feasibility/floors/dependencies. Joint endorsement promotes the proposal; otherwise the lead revises, up to 3 rounds, then it is promoted with the unresolved findings. The approval card offers Approve / Request refinement / Reject and a View PRD link for the paired revision. Decisions are idempotent. Publication persists the approval and preflights repo access. It creates every issue held (draft title, held label, stable plan-ID marker), reads each back, reconciles lost creates by marker, wires hierarchy and dependencies, verifies, then releases the implementation issues. Approved blockers are enforced on both auto-assign and explicit starts. Demo fixtures, unit tests and e2e specs come with each slice.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream main 157efde has no ideas/PRD/proposal/publication code (no server/ideas*.ts, proposals.ts, publication.ts, issuePlan.ts, approvedBlockers.ts, shared/ideaReview.ts). Its CEO can only file_issue / set_dependencies directly.
features.rfc_relation: workflows; spec/review; approvals; multi-repo (cross-floor issue plans)
features.rationale: This is the closest existing implementation of the RFC's plan -> spec -> independent review -> human approval -> build pipeline. Its core rules are pure, tested modules (shared/ideaReview.ts, server/issuePlan.ts, proposals.ts, publication.ts, approvedBlockers.ts, ideaResearch.ts, ideaWorkflow.ts) that can be lifted almost verbatim. The ~1000 lines of swarm.ts glue must be rewritten: pickReviewers chooses reviewers by role (researcher/qa/dev), which upstream removed, and new state has to go through upstream's outbox patches and fit scale.test budgets. Suggested order: pure modules and tests, then glue with demo fakes, then the UI.
features.risks: Publication creates issues on GitHub. The held-label + draft-title + read-back discipline must be kept, or plans could leak into scheduling half-published. Research sessions use web access. The fork's own spec says end-to-end acceptance against real GitHub credentials was still open. It is GitHub-only (issue markers, labels), so non-GitHub trackers need an adapter behind Backend.

features.title: Researchers: a lobby researcher and per-floor researchers file web research as dated Markdown docs by PR (company-wide docs in a 'cubebase' repo)
features.description: A researcher role. The lobby researcher works a queue of briefs from the manager or the CEO's request_research tool. Floor researchers take swarm:research issues. They research with WebSearch/WebFetch, write docs/research/<date>-<slug>.md plus a README index line, and open a PR that skips QA (the office auto-merges it when checks pass if the floor allows it). Company-wide research goes to a cubebase repository. Includes a research desk UI in the lobby. It is also the session runner behind the Ideas research, plan, review and revise phases.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no research.ts and no researcher role. Upstream a277839 (#288) made all agents interchangeable with no roles.
features.rationale: Useful as a 'research' task kind that any free agent can take, and needed by the Ideas workflow. Port the prompts and job model (server/research.ts is mostly pure) rather than the role, since upstream dropped roles.
features.risks: Web access from unsandboxed sessions. Research PRs skip QA and may auto-merge. Needs an extra company repository.

features.title: Prototype issues: disposable draft-PR experiments the manager approves into an implementation issue or sends back with feedback
features.description: Prototype issues go to a developer with a prototype playbook (vendored cubebase-prototype skill). The developer builds the smallest runnable experiment on a prototype branch and opens a draft PR with fixed headings (Question and scope, How to run and review, Screenshots, Findings and limitations). The source issue stays open. The manager reviews from the Kanban Blocked column. Approve, pinned to the reviewed head SHA, turns the prototype issue into an implementation issue with a new title and body. Revise sends feedback back to the same draft. The same commit moves company research filing into the cubebase repo.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No prototype concept in upstream: no prototype labels, playbook or approve/revise endpoints in server/ or client/.
features.rationale: A spike -> human decision -> real issue loop is a natural factory stage and cheap compared with the Ideas workflow. The playbook and endpoint logic are small. The glue sits in swarm.ts and the Kanban, which both diverged heavily.
features.risks: Agents push prototype branches and draft PRs. Approval rewrites the issue body. Depends on a vendored third-party skill (MIT).

features.title: Manager MCP gateway: external agents drive the office as the manager over authenticated Streamable HTTP (/mcp)
features.description: A separate /mcp endpoint (apart from the per-agent /api/mcp/:token). It uses a bearer token, stored only as a verifier and compared with timingSafeEqual, an on/off switch in Settings, and a CUBEFARM_MCP_TOKEN env/config-file fallback. Browser-origin requests are rejected, and the gateway is enabled only when the office runs from a checkout on main. Tools: office status and full snapshot, read/send phone messages with idempotent UUID receipts, and decisions on CEO staffing proposals. #343 adds parity with console commands: agents (stop, reset, assign, message, dismiss, update, screen), floors (add, connect, update, remove, sync, plan, onboard), PRs (merge, close, run QA), prototypes, office close/reopen/update, settings, ideas, research and publication retry.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream only serves the CEO's office tools to its own sessions at POST /api/mcp/:token (server/index.ts:39). There is no manager-level external MCP endpoint.
features.rfc_relation: security; approvals (external control plane for an orchestrating agent)
features.rationale: This makes the factory scriptable from Claude Desktop/Code or another orchestrator. managerMcp.ts is a thin, well-shaped adapter over Swarm methods. Port the gateway and settings, map its tools onto upstream's existing Swarm methods, and leave out fleet, telegram, ideas and prototype tools until those features exist. managerMcpSettings has unit tests. managerMcp.ts itself is only covered by an e2e spec.
features.risks: One bearer token grants full manager power: merge PRs, remove floors, close the office. Destructive annotations are advisory only. It must stay loopback-only or sit behind a TLS proxy that exposes only /mcp. Token storage moves to a separate settings file.

features.title: Refuse cross-origin websocket upgrades on /ws and /ws/term
features.description: server/wsOrigin.ts allowUpgrade(origin, host, hostnames): the Origin must equal the Host the request came in on and be a loopback name, or, when SWARM_HOST is not loopback, one of the bound/LAN interface addresses or the hostname. 'null' and non-http origins are refused. A missing Origin (a non-browser client) is accepted. Refused origins are logged once. This blocks cross-site websocket hijacking and DNS rebinding of /ws/term, which types into unsandboxed agent CLIs.
features.already_upstream_evidence: The upstream server/index.ts upgrade handler (lines ~346-351) routes /ws and /ws/term to handleUpgrade with no Origin check. No Origin handling exists anywhere in server/*.ts. Upstream f32ce7d (#305) lets the office listen beyond 127.0.0.1, which makes the gap more exposed.
features.rationale: wsOrigin.ts and its 68-line test are self-contained. Only ~10 lines of the upstream upgrade handler need a hand-merge, next to its upgradeGateway branch. It closes a real hole in a cheap, well-tested way.
features.risks: Upstream's preview gateway (8ebd6c3, #310) serves agent-built preview apps under /preview/<port>/ on the office's own origin. A malicious preview page is same-origin and still passes this check, so the gateway's origin model needs its own follow-up.

features.title: Security review stage: QA screens every merge candidate and escalates security-boundary PRs to a dedicated security-audit QA session that holds the merge
features.description: Ordinary QA runs a pr-security-review skill on merge candidates. When a PR touches authn/authz, tenant isolation, secrets or untrusted input to privileged operations, QA sets securityReviewReason. The office then labels the PR (READY_FOR_SECURITY_REVIEW) and assigns a fresh QA session with the security playbook. That session uses the vendored Cloudflare security-audit skill with coverage-ledger and findings validators and a JSON report schema. The merge (and the merge queue) stays held until the specialist passes the current head. Removing the label waives the review, incomplete audits are named, passes survive disjoint base advances, and the review can run without a desk sandbox.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/swarm.ts has no security-related code (grep 'security' finds nothing). There is no security label, playbook or skill.
features.rationale: A risk-triggered extra review gate is exactly the kind of configurable stage the factory needs. The office-side change is moderate (label, hold, extra QA kind). Most of the ~7k lines are vendored skill content that can be copied as-is. It needs adapting to upstream's role-less QA and merge gate.
features.risks: Vendored third-party skill (MIT, Cloudflare) with .cjs validators that agents execute. Adds paid sessions for every security-touching PR. A label-based waiver lets anyone with repo write access skip the review.

features.title: Release-shipped agent skills and file-backed specialism playbooks (developer, QA, security, prototype) for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
features.description: server/repoSkills.ts validates skills/<name>/SKILL.md (names, frontmatter, no nested manifests) and loads the bundle into memory at startup. The bundle ships in the npm package. Each runtime gets it its own way: a local plugin via --plugin-dir for Claude Code, the plugin option for the Agent SDK, a skill dir in OpenCode's per-process config, and for Codex a copy in .agents/skills/cubefarm-bundle inside the desk, with a git exclude and an ownership marker. docs/specialisms/{developer,qa,security,prototype}.md playbooks are injected at session launch by task kind and name which skills to invoke and how per runtime. Vendored MIT skills: tdd, diagnosing-bugs, code-review, verification-before-completion, test-strategy, humanizer, ponytail-review, codebase-design, implement, browser-proxy-resolve, cubebase-prototype.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no skills/ directory and no specialism or playbook mechanism (grep for specialty/specialism/playbook in server/shared finds only journal.ts). Prompts are built inline from floor mission/brief.
features.rfc_relation: workflows (artifact-driven stage playbooks); model routing (per-runtime registration)
features.rationale: Versioned, per-stage playbooks and skills shipped with the release are the backbone of configurable workflows, and the mechanism is runtime-agnostic. repoSkills.ts is self-contained. The launch-path changes in cliRunner/clis/agentRunner need re-applying to upstream's newer launch code. The vendored skills can be curated rather than taken wholesale.
features.risks: Third-party skill content (all MIT, attributions kept) changes agent behaviour on every floor. Larger npm package. Codex bundle copying writes into project worktrees (relies on .git/info/exclude).

features.title: Revision-pinned QA outcomes, findings tracked by ID across rounds, CI-evidence reuse, repo-specific QA guidance (CUBEBASE_QA.md) and opted-in inline suggestions
features.description: QA outcomes are recorded against the exact tested head SHA, and legacy penalties are gated. Findings get stable IDs and are carried forward, so follow-up rounds only re-check what changed plus the open findings. QA prints a 'Blast radius' and 'Coverage gap' lines and reuses trusted, successful commit-pinned CI jobs as evidence. Green CI is accepted for environment-only blockers. A worker running out of memory counts as a resource failure, not a charged round. QA reads a root CUBEBASE_QA.md for repository-specific rules. It triages current Codex-connector P1/P2 review threads, and confirmed non-blockers become follow-up issues filed after merge. Opted-in inline suggestions can be applied by QA and re-queued. A durable QA history panel is included. swarm/issue-339-ada (closed PR #341) is an earlier variant superseded by #340.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream 5c3f021 (#127) 'QA trusts GitHub's checks and re-tests focus on what changed' covers CI trust and narrowed re-tests. There are no finding IDs, revision-pinned outcome records, CUBEBASE_QA.md or suggestion-applying QA upstream.
features.rationale: Pinning verdicts to SHAs and carrying findings by ID makes the review gate auditable and cheaper per round. A per-repo QA guidance file fits artifact-driven workflows. qaFindings.ts and qaEvidence.ts are pure and portable, but most behaviour is spread through swarm.ts prompts and report handling.
features.risks: Letting QA push applied suggestions breaks upstream's rule that QA leaves GitHub alone. The Codex-connector thread triage assumes a specific third-party review bot.

features.title: Merge queue: QA-approved PRs are queued and rebased server-side with tree verification before merge
features.description: Instead of GitHub's update-branch, the office computes the expected merge tree locally (workspace.mergeQueueTree). It calls GraphQL updatePullRequestBranch with updateMethod REBASE and expectedHeadOid, and accepts the result only if the base ref is unchanged and the new head's tree equals the expected tree. PRs labelled needs-human, needs-review or security-review, and drafts, are skipped. Failed CI jobs are re-run once (gh run rerun --failed) and approved PRs merge in order. #299 verifies against live target refs.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream only has updateBranch (server/github.ts:216, backend.ts:37) and a merge-method fallback loop in swarm.ts:1631. No queue and no verified rebase.
features.rationale: The parallel-agent factory merges many PRs, and a verified rebase-then-merge queue avoids stale-base merges without force-pushing from local clones. rebasePull is self-contained. The queue ordering lives in swarm.ts and must be rewired into upstream's merge loop.
features.risks: Rewrites PR branch history (rebase) automatically. Relies on GitHub-specific GraphQL mutations, so non-GitHub hosts need another path.

features.title: CEO merge_pr with explicit manager approval, merge preflight against the tested head, and human follow-up issues
features.description: The CEO can merge a PR only after the manager approves it in the phone. mergePr.ts never merges an unseen head: it requires a completed QA report at exactly the tested SHA (later extended to incomplete reports posted at that head, and to incomplete security audits at the current head). It can file human follow-up issues and reference them in the merge comment.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream CEO tools are company_status, agent_detail, set_floor_profile, scale_team, configure_agent, file_issue, set_dependencies, close_issue, retry_qa, send_back, rerun_checks, close_pull and escalate. There is no merge tool.
features.rationale: A human-approved override path for PRs stuck behind an incomplete gate is useful. The head-pinned preflight (mergePr.ts, pure) is the valuable part. Port it as a manager action first and as a CEO tool only behind an explicit approval record.
features.risks: An LLM performs merges based on a chat approval. If the approval capture is loose, this bypasses QA.

features.title: Extra CEO office tools: start_issue, park_pr, route_issue (ready-for-human), connect_floor, explicit triage flag, comment_issue, close as completed, stuck-PR reasons
features.description: New CEO tools. start_issue makes an explicit assignment. park_pr atomically parks blocked placeholder PRs behind issue gates. route_issue sets or clears ready-for-human. connect_floor connects a repo with automation options. A triage flag marks issues as triaged. comment_issue posts on an open issue and forwards the comment into any live session on it. close_issue gains completed:true. company_status explains why a PR is stuck while staying small. Also send_back_to_dev and rerun QA (fork #33/#22). swarm/issue-25-grace is an unmerged earlier send_back_to_dev attempt, superseded by #33 in main.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has retry_qa, send_back and close_issue (c7c81be #177), equivalent to fork #22/#33 and part of #285. start_issue, park_pr, route_issue, connect_floor, comment_issue and the triage flag are absent from upstream server/ceo.ts.
features.rationale: Pick the small, high-leverage tools (comment_issue, start_issue, route_issue, park_pr). Each is a zod tool plus a Swarm method and a demo fake, and they port tool by tool. Skip the duplicates of upstream tools.
features.risks: Grows the CEO's prompt and tool surface, which costs paid tokens every session (upstream CLAUDE.md asks for short prompts).

features.title: Scheduling gates: ready-for-human label, draft/untriaged issues, parent issues, duplicate-claim prevention, empty-session backoff, persisted explicit starts
features.description: readyIssues/auto-assign skip issues labelled ready-for-human (a manual assign gets a 409, and company_status marks them), draft or untriaged issues, and parent issues that have sub-issues. Consecutive no-work sessions back off until the manager or owner changes the brief (issueWork.ts). An issue-claims registry (issueClaims.ts) stops two desks claiming the same issue across assign, resume and reconnect. Explicit starts survive office restarts (requestedStarts.ts).
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream shared/issues.ts has swarm:skip, 'Depends on #N' parsing and hold-up ranking, plus bff498b (#106) so merged issues are not handed out again. Grepping upstream for ready-for-human, untriaged, parent/sub-issue rules and claim registries finds nothing.
features.rationale: Label-driven human gates and triage gates are core governance for an autonomous factory and are mostly pure predicates. The claim registry fixes a real double-assignment class of bug. They have to be re-applied to upstream's rewritten scheduler (interchangeable agents).
features.risks: Label names become a contract with users' repos. A mis-set label silently starves the queue, so it needs visible reasons in the UI.

features.title: Native GitHub issue dependencies (blockedBy) and sub-issues: fail-closed scheduling and auto-closing finished parents
features.description: listIssues reads GraphQL blockedBy and subIssuesSummary. If the host or token lacks those fields it retries without them and falls back to body 'Depends on' text. It fails closed when dependency reads fail and keeps partial results. Developers blocked without a PR are released after checking that the remote branch is absent. Each sync closes an open parent whose sub-issues are all done (once per sub-issue count, with a comment, toast and message), skipping parents an open PR closes, parents being worked on, and those with a keep-open label.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream only parses 'Depends on #N' / 'Blocked by #N' text from issue bodies (shared/issues.ts:3-42). Grepping upstream server/github.ts and shared/issues.ts finds no blockedBy, subIssues or parent handling.
features.rfc_relation: workflows; multi-repo (cross-repo dependencies and tracking parents)
features.rationale: Native dependency and hierarchy data is what multi-repo plans (and the Ideas publication) need, and the fail-closed handling is careful. Mostly server/github.ts plus shared/issues.ts, which changed less upstream than swarm.ts.
features.risks: GitHub-specific GraphQL fields (issue dependencies and sub-issues), so non-GitHub trackers need an adapter. Auto-closing parents writes to GitHub.

features.title: Run history: durable per-attempt records with routing factors, CLI/model/effort, playbook hash, worker health, revisions and cost, exportable as JSON
features.description: Every attempt (issue, prototype, research, QA run, fix) is recorded in its own file, so QA cleanup and restarts leave it intact. Each record has a parent chain from the issue attempt through QA rounds and repairs to the merge. It records why the attempt went to that desk (manager/ceo/auto/qa-queue/repair/retry/resume) and the routing factors, the requested CLI/model/effort, the playbook name@sha256, office version, worker and its health at start and end, starting and submitted commits, session ids, times (queueMs/runMs) and usage (sessions, cost, turns, with null when unknown). Prompts and transcripts are never stored. The data shows in a Kanban panel and at GET /api/run-history?repoId=&issue=&pr=&download=1.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream keeps only a cumulative costUsd per agent (server/swarm.ts:156, 3061) and a time-lapse journal of broadcasts (server/journal.ts). It has no per-attempt history with model/effort/routing data.
features.rfc_relation: cost telemetry; model routing (evidence for routing by CLI/model/effort)
features.rationale: Per-attempt cost and outcome data keyed by model and runtime is the foundation for cost budgets and model routing. runHistory.ts is self-contained. Hooking attempt start/end into upstream's session lifecycle is the main work.
features.risks: Grows state on disk and needs pruning. The CLIs don't report the model actually used, and Codex/OpenCode have no cost.

features.title: Developer Authorship and Repair scores from verified outcomes, used to rank assignment (specialty first)
features.description: An append-only score ledger derived from PR contribution and QA histories. Authorship credits verified first-pass work and Repair credits independently verified fixes. Original PR authorship is preserved across repair handoffs (prContributions.ts). Score chips appear in the team and terminal headers, with a score history. Assignment policy specialty-first-v2 ranks eligible developers by specialty, then Authorship or Repair, then workload.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no scores or feedback modules. Upstream agents are interchangeable (a277839, #288) and routing is not outcome-based.
features.rationale: Ranking named agents conflicts with upstream's interchangeable agents. The useful idea is to score CLI/model/effort combinations from verified outcomes and feed routing, built on run history rather than ported as is.
features.risks: Gamable or noisy metrics can starve agents. The ledger logic is intricate.

features.title: Reviewed lessons from recurring QA findings and playbook evaluations against pinned attempts and comparable cohorts
features.description: Lessons are reviewed guidance drafted from recurring QA findings (the same finding key on several PRs) or from recoveries. Each one links redacted sources, verification (a fix or regression test plus a passing QA outcome or attempt), and revisions, and goes through Approve / Send back / Reject / Revise. Playbook evaluations compare a base and a candidate playbook hash on a pinned case and on live cohorts from run history, using metrics such as first-pass QA and verified repair. Results are saved as immutable reports and flag confounded comparisons. The office never rewrites prompts automatically.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No lessons or evaluations modules upstream.
features.rfc_relation: model routing / playbook evaluation; spec/review feedback loop
features.rationale: The concept (human-reviewed lessons and A/B evaluation of playbooks) fits a self-improving factory. It depends on run history, QA findings and specialisms all being ported first, so treat it as a later phase.
features.risks: Secret redaction heuristics guard what enters lessons. The UI is heavy for the value.

features.title: Browser dashboard alongside the 3D office: per-agent terminal tiles, floor activity, lobby work list, office notices, full manager console
features.description: A desktop 2D view (client/src/ui/Dashboard.tsx + dashboard.css) as an alternative to the 3D office. It shows a grid of agent tiles with live terminal or SDK output, expandable to the full terminal, floor activity, who is working, office-wide notices shared with the HUD, and the full manager console, Kanban and phone, all on the same store and websocket data.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has pocket mode (client/src/pocket/, 2D office for phones, 048a6c2 #237), FloorList list view (214a0d8 #257) and mission-control lobby dashboards (b8a2994 #245). It has no desktop terminal-grid dashboard.
features.rationale: A dense, non-3D operator view with every terminal on one screen is useful for a factory, and it is mostly client-only. It must be rebuilt on upstream's newer store, outbox watch (shared/watch.ts) and Panel components rather than copied.
features.risks: Showing many live terminals at once raises websocket traffic, which upstream's watch/outbox logic deliberately limits.

features.title: Fleet: run agents' desks and CLIs on other machines over SSH ('boxes'), floor/agent placement, version sync and a Fleet tab
features.description: A Machine/CliHost seam (server/machine.ts, localCliHost.ts, cliFiles.ts). The office runs `ssh <dest> cubefarm box --stdio` (boxLink.ts/boxStdio.ts/boxOps.ts) on LAN or tailnet machines, which start their own terminal keeper. Desks, CLI session files and screenshots live on the box, and hooks relay back over the link, so dropped SSH links reattach. The manager adds and removes boxes and puts a whole floor or single agents on a box, applied at the next session start. Boxes are kept on the office's commit or release (`cubefarm box --update`, no drain unless the keeper changed), with Check again and a retry for failed moves. CLIs are found in installer folders. Opt-in forwarding of the office Claude credential is available. A Fleet tab is included.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream a277839 (#288) introduced server/machines.ts MachineProvider (local folders), and b8469a6 (#309) added Upstash Box cloud agents (boxMachines.ts, boxCli.ts). There is no SSH/LAN worker provider upstream.
features.rfc_relation: multi-repo / distributed execution; cost (use own hardware)
features.rationale: Running agents on your own servers is valuable for an on-prem factory. The fork's seam predates and differs from upstream's MachineProvider, so the SSH box should be rebuilt as a third provider next to local and Upstash, reusing boxStdio/boxLink ideas. Do not merge the fork's machine.ts.
features.risks: Remote command execution over SSH. Self-updating remote checkouts (git fetch/merge/build on workers). Optional forwarding of a Claude subscription credential to workers. Cross-OS shell quirks. The term 'box' clashes with upstream's Upstash Box.

features.title: Machine resource diagnosis and capacity advice (CPU/memory/IO pressure via PSI, reboot-required signals) plus scheduled unattended worker upgrades
features.description: The office and every box are sampled every 5 s (machineResources.ts). machineHealth.ts separates busy from confirmed contention using Linux PSI, load versus CPU count, macOS pressure, and RAM headroom. The manager declares whether each machine is fixed or resizable, and the Fleet tab gives advice (move work, resize, reduce concurrency) without acting on it. rebootStatus.ts reads OS restart signals. scripts/cron-office-update.mjs and install-maintenance-cron.mjs schedule unattended office and worker upgrades, including while the office stays closed.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no machineResources/machineHealth/rebootStatus modules and no cron maintenance scripts. Its self-update runs only through the launcher (scripts/office.mjs, server/officeUpdate.ts).
features.rationale: Resource-pressure advice is useful once multiple workers exist, but it depends on the fleet. The unattended cron auto-upgrade conflicts with upstream's manager-triggered update model.
features.risks: Unattended auto-update (git pull + build + restart) on a schedule. The cron script calls the office API on 127.0.0.1:4317 and hard-codes the fork's repo name.

features.title: Disposable Upstash Box workers with durable task reservations and an Upstash key in Settings
features.description: The fork's own take on cloud workers. A disposable Upstash Box per task runs the box keeper over a stdio bridge. upstash.ts records task reservations before provider writes so uncertain creates stay recoverable, and boxes are cleaned up when tasks end. Includes a write-only Box API key setting, OpenCode v2 pinned in worker boxes, and docs for validating a worker end to end. swarm/issue-287-ada (closed PR #289) was superseded by #288.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream b8469a6 (#309) 'Cloud agents: an Upstash Box each, signed in at their desk' independently implements Upstash cloud agents (server/cloud.ts, box.ts, boxMachines.ts, boxScripts.ts, boxCli.ts) with keys in secrets.json.
features.rationale: It duplicates upstream's cloud agents in a different, incompatible design. The only idea worth carrying over is the durable 'reserve before provider write' task record in server/upstash.ts, applied to upstream's boxMachines.
features.risks: External paid service and an API key. Task credentials are sent into cloud VMs.

features.title: Remote Claude subscription sign-in from Settings (setup-token in a private PTY) and forwarding the office token to trusted SSH workers
features.description: Settings -> Claude authentication runs the official CLI's `setup-token` in a private, bounded PTY (claudeAuth.ts, claudeSetup.ts). The manager opens the sign-in link on a phone and pastes the code back, or uses a manual token fallback. The fork keeps CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in new Claude sessions and can forward it over SSH to workers listed in CUBEFARM_CLAUDE_AUTH_BOXES. Real auth actions require CUBEFARM_AUTH_ORIGIN behind an authenticated HTTPS nginx proxy.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has `cubefarm login` (bin/cubefarm.js) and cloud agents signing in with their CLI's own login at the desk (cliRunner.ts startBoxSignIn). Upstream strips CLAUDE_* from agent env and never captures a setup token.
features.rationale: It handles a long-lived subscription credential, contradicts upstream's env stripping policy, and only matters for the fork's remote/SSH setup. Upstream's sign-in-at-desk approach is safer.
features.risks: Captures and stores a long-lived Claude OAuth token, injects it into sessions and forwards it to other machines. Depends on scraping CLI TUI output. Possible subscription terms-of-use issues with remote use.

features.title: Telegram mirror of the manager-CEO phone conversation, with proposal buttons and a private config file for secrets
features.description: One paired private Telegram chat mirrors the phone in both directions, using Bot API long polling (no webhook). Pairing is confirmed locally with the user and chat ids. A durable ordered outbox splits long replies. Approve/Reject buttons on staffing proposals call the same guarded commands as the console. The bot token lives in ~/.config/cubefarm/.env (bin/officeCredentials.js, docs/configuration.md) and is kept out of agent and preview env.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream 6088764 (#274) removed Discord/Slack/Telegram notifications, and server/notifier.ts now deletes saved chat-app tokens. Notifications are desktop and Web Push only.
features.rationale: Remote approvals from chat are a reasonable idea. The manager MCP gateway plus upstream's PWA/Web Push cover most of the need with less surface, and upstream deliberately dropped chat apps.
features.risks: External service, a bot token, and inbound commands from the internet (mitigated by pairing).

features.title: Paste images into prompts, issues and briefs for local and remote agents
features.description: Clipboard images pasted into a PromptTextarea are stored by the office outside project history (attachments.ts, imageRoutes.ts) and referenced as ordinary links, so every existing prompt, issue and brief can carry them. Remote boxes receive verified copies over SSH. A manager MCP prepare_image_prompt tool is also added.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no attachment storage or image routes. Clipboard use in client/src/ui is only copy-to-clipboard and the AppViewer iframe allow list.
features.rationale: Giving agents screenshots and mockups is valuable for a visual factory. The server side is small. The box-copy part should target upstream's MachineProvider (local + Upstash) instead.
features.risks: Stores user images on disk and serves them over HTTP, so size limits and the path traversal checks must be kept.

features.title: Close Office: a persistent admission hold that drains running jobs before shutdown, and reopen
features.description: The manager can close the office. New work is held across all floors and survives restarts, running jobs drain, and the console shows when it is safe to shut down. Reopen resumes the held work, and deferred recovery is retained until the resume succeeds.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream drains only for its own self-update (server/officeUpdate.ts, swarm.ts:588 drainingSince, 4029 officeUpdateTick) and paces new work on usage warnings (server/pacing.ts). It has no manual, persistent close.
features.rfc_relation: cost/usage budget (manual stop of spend); approvals
features.rationale: A factory-wide 'stop taking new work' switch is basic operational control and can reuse upstream's existing drain machinery.
features.risks: A forgotten closed state silently stops all work, so the UI must keep it visible.

features.title: Apply per-agent model changes to kept-alive CLIs; remember each CLI's default model
features.description: #322: a CLI waiting at its prompt is adopted for the next session only if its model matches the requested one. Otherwise it is closed and restarted, and the model is persisted in keeper metadata. #123: settings.defaultModels keeps a default model per coding agent, so switching the office's default CLI and back does not lose a typed Codex or OpenCode model.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/cliRunner.ts:482 adopts a waiting CLI on reattach or cli+resumeId only, ignoring the model, so the same bug is present. Upstream swarm.ts:3710 resets defaultModel whenever defaultCli changes.
features.rationale: These are small fixes to real upstream bugs, and both are prerequisites for reliable per-task model routing. Re-implement them against upstream's cliRunner adopt check and settings.
features.risks: None notable. Restarting a CLI on a model change loses its warm context.

features.title: Shared Docker-engine safety rules in developer, QA, prototype and security prompts
features.description: Adds one block to every agent system prompt. It says the Docker engine is shared with other desks and the manager, and tells agents to record and remove only the containers, networks and volumes they created, by ID. Agents must never rm/stop/kill by name pattern, label or filter, never prune, and never run compose down on projects they did not create, and should leave anything with an unclear owner and report it. Tests assert it reaches every prompt kind and runtime, and that it keeps Codex's command line under 8000 characters.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream prompts have no Docker guidance (grep 'docker' in server/ finds only shared/activity.ts).
features.rationale: Unsandboxed parallel agents on one machine can destroy each other's or the manager's containers. These few lines are cheap insurance. Copy the text into upstream's prompt builders.
features.risks: Adds tokens to every session prompt.

features.title: Claude Code terminal-session robustness: missing hooks, stalled or crashed startups, permission/Bash-expansion prompts, bypass mode, restart turn collection, desk recovery
features.description: Ends Claude sessions whose hooks never reach the office and tells that apart from 'not started'. Recovers sessions that stall before startup, so CLI startup crashes don't exhaust task budgets. Collects turns completed while the office was restarting. Keeps active tools alive during recovery. Recovers office-MCP approval screens when hooks are missed and answers Claude's Bash-expansion prompt. Starts unattended desks with --permission-mode bypassPermissions. Recovers desks automatically after office or CLI failures. Resumes PR repairs with the CLI that created the session. Fixes startup menu selection for reused sessions. Adds cancellation through desk helpers (operation.ts) and transcript-based recovery evidence (cliTranscript.ts).
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream e38a6da (#275) adds startup reconciliation and a stuck-work watchdog. Upstream keeps CLIs alive across restarts via the keeper and answers permissions through the PreToolUse hook with --permission-mode acceptEdits (server/clis.ts:252). The fork's specific screen answers, hookless detection, restart turn collection and bypass mode are absent.
features.rationale: Each fix targets failure modes seen in long unattended runs, but they are written against the fork's diverged cliRunner/ptyHost. Reproduce each symptom on upstream first and port only what still happens there. Skip bypassPermissions, which goes against upstream's hook-based design.
features.risks: bypassPermissions removes Claude's own permission layer. Auto-answering TUI prompts is brittle across CLI versions.

features.title: Codex and OpenCode runtime fixes: turn-end detection, safety refusals, menus, hooks-review prompt, long command lines, OpenCode v2 completion and model config
features.description: Codex: model display name normalization. Sessions keep running until the main thread's turn ends, and sessions cut off mid-task are not dropped. Threads resume in the agent's own desk, and sessions stuck at a menu end. Sessions stalled after safety refusals end. The 'Hooks need review' question is answered whenever it appears. Long instructions move into a file to keep the command line short. A Playwright transport config collision is fixed. OpenCode: model selection through inline config, v2 completion reporting and lost-turn recovery (opencodeTranscript.ts).
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream handles Codex hook trust (server/cliRunner.ts:181, server/clis.ts:229) and passes OpenCode config via OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (cliRunner.ts:895, clis.ts:212). Upstream has no Codex command-length guard and no OpenCode v2 completion handling.
features.rationale: Multi-runtime support is central to model and cost routing, and these fixes come with captured screen fixtures (server/fixtures/codexScreens.ts, opencodeScreens.ts) that are reusable for tests. Port them per symptom after checking that upstream still has each bug.
features.risks: Fixes are tied to specific CLI versions (Codex v0.166, OpenCode v2.0.32).

features.title: PR check reads via Actions runs and a commit-status REST fallback; per-resource refresh health
features.description: When statusCheckRollup is inaccessible, PR checks are read through Actions runs and the commit status REST API (checkRuns.ts carries run IDs for reruns). Repository sync keeps working when checks can't be read. repoRefresh.ts keeps independent successes and last-success timestamps per GitHub resource, shown in a RepoRefreshStatus panel.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream 2491d2e (#292) explains gh/git failures and retries board reads once, but still relies only on statusCheckRollup (server/github.ts:86-94).
features.rationale: Reliable check reads are needed for an automated merge gate and work with fine-grained tokens that lack checks:read. Mostly confined to github.ts.
features.risks: More GitHub API calls and rate-limit pressure.

features.title: Agent environment hygiene: strip the office's npm script policy, keep package registries reachable, delete disposable job scratch
features.description: projectEnv.ts removes the npm_config allow-scripts policy that `npm run` exports, which npm rejects in project-scoped installs, from agent, preview and folder-sync environments, and keeps gateway credentials out. Agent test runs keep registries reachable. jobScratch.ts gives each development or QA job a disposable scratch folder that is deleted when the job finishes.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream strips ANTHROPIC_*/CLAUDE_* from agent and preview env. Upstream package.json declares no allowScripts policy, so the npm inheritance bug is mostly fork-specific. Upstream has no per-job scratch folder.
features.rationale: The npm policy fix only matters if we adopt the fork's allowScripts setting. The job-scratch and 'gateway credentials never enter agent env' rules are worth reapplying when the related features are ported.
features.risks: None notable.

features.title: QA loop policies: re-runs don't spend QA's budget, crashed fixes go to another developer, QA-passed drafts are marked ready, conflicts recovered and failed CI retried once
features.description: QA rounds that are re-runs don't count against the budget. A crashed fix session hands the PR to another developer. A draft PR that passed QA is marked ready (gh pr ready) instead of waiting forever. QA conflicts are recovered and failed CI is retried once before a PR is sent back.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream 2fc43e2 (#140, a conflict alone never goes to the manager), 9ab8a50 (#176, re-run a flaky check) and 8311a00 (#181, developers own their PR with bigger budgets) cover most of this. Marking QA-passed drafts ready is absent upstream (no markPullReady in server/github.ts).
features.rationale: Upstream reached equivalent policies independently. Only the draft-to-ready step is new, and it is a one-function idea to fold into the merge-queue port.
features.risks: None notable.

features.title: Expanded Kanban stages: backlog / to-do / in progress / QA / review / ready / merged / blocked
features.description: Splits the five-column board into readiness-aware stages. Backlog holds issues that are not ready (issueReadinessReason). To-do holds ready issues. Review holds QA-passed PRs waiting on a needs-review label. Blocked holds needs-human issues or PRs. The whiteboard drawing and terminal headers are updated to match.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream client/src/store.ts:714 still returns the five columns { backlog, progress, qa, ready, merged }.
features.rationale: A board that shows the governance stages (needs review, blocked on a human) is what makes the factory's workflow visible. Small client and shared changes, though upstream's whiteboard 2.0 (ad54db5) also uses these columns.
features.risks: Upstream's whiteboard, pocket mode and mission control all consume the column set, so changing it touches several views.

features.title: Hand-rewritten backports of upstream fixes (session existence, hand-out, gh error text, reportless QA, real paths, fix-push check, orphan QA, closed-work stop, desk reset, outline leak, DPR, preview env size, Playwright MCP pin, SWARM_HOST)
features.description: Fork commits that re-implement fixes that later or concurrently landed upstream. They are listed so nothing is silently dropped.

features.title: Fork CI on self-hosted LAN runners, artifact retention script, consolidated tests, e2e Node 24 pin, test isolation fixes

It reviews and posts committable code suggestions using an OPENROUTER_API_KEY secret, without checking out PR code. QA's playbook can then apply opted-in suggestions.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream .github/workflows has only ci.yml and release.yml.
features.rfc_relation: spec/review (independent second-model review); model routing (cheap reviewer model)

method_notes:
Partial clone of mgscox/cubefarm at C:/Users/peti/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c968d675ef2f985c/23326b94-69a1-40d9-887d-ac86b5b528d8/scratchpad/forks/mgscox with upstream/main fetched (157efde). Merge base 11237cf (Release 0.3.2, 2026-10-01). Fork main is 213 ahead and 135 behind, with ~59k added lines in 487 files. Nothing from the fork was built or run.

Branches: all 94 remote refs were listed and mapped to the fork's 190 PRs via `gh pr list -R mgscox/cubefarm` (186 merged, 4 closed). For every merged branch, I checked that the tip commit time is not later than the PR's mergedAt (none were), so every merged branch is fully represented in fork main. They are reported only under the feature they belong to.

The unmerged branches contain no unique work, so none gets its own feature:
- swarm/issue-339-ada (closed #341): superseded by #340 (9040800).
- swarm/issue-287-ada (closed #289): superseded by #288 (5e16305).
- swarm/issue-221-linus (closed #223): superseded by #222 (9d2bc9e).
- fix/e2e-skip-tour-pointer-lock (closed #80): superseded by #88 (ac71f45).
- swarm/issue-25-grace (no PR): an earlier send_back_to_dev, superseded by #33 (38ea922).

Skipped as evidence-only:
- 11 screenshot branches (swarm/issue-*-screenshots, *-shots).
- swarm-qa-evidence (1332 commits of QA screenshots).
- claude/fleet-console, claude/fleet-floor-box, claude/sleepy-haslett-d700c4, fix/codex-playwright-config, fix/preview-npm-allow-scripts and swarm/issue-1-linus: these have empty diffs against fork main.

Detecting work already in fork main: git here is 2.33, which has no `merge-tree --write-tree`. I used `git apply --cached -R --check` of each branch's patch against a temporary index of origin/main. Many branches failed only because main later edited the same lines, so PR merge state was the deciding evidence.

Detecting work already upstream: fork main vs upstream was not compared mechanically, since both sides changed ~3k lines of swarm.ts plus cliRunner, ceo, demo and types. I judged it by:
- reading upstream code in the user's worktree (grep for the relevant modules, functions and labels);
- comparing commit titles;
- the fork's own docs/research/2026-11-04-upstream-pr-port-review.md, which maps 18 fork commits to upstream PRs. I spot-checked those mappings against upstream commit titles. The doc is data, not instructions.

Depth: I read docs, module header comments, the key pure modules in full (shared/ideaReview.ts, server/ideaWorkflow.ts, ideaResearch.ts, research.ts, wsOrigin.ts, the start of managerMcp.ts, rebasePull in github.ts, part of repoSkills.ts, the docs/specialisms QA and prototype playbooks, pr-agent.yml, the ci.yml diff, and the Backend interface diff), plus per-commit stats and bodies. I did not read every line of the 59k-line diff. In particular, the swarm.ts glue for each feature was judged from commit stats and tests, not a line-by-line review.

Line and file counts are summed per commit, excluding screenshots. They may double count where both a branch's individual commits and its squash landed on main (the fleet phases, #79/#81/#83). Images and screenshots were not inspected. Vendored skill content was not reviewed beyond licence headers and skills/README.md.

Main caveat for any import: the fork keeps explicit roles (dev, qa, researcher, ceo) and its own Machine/box seam, and upstream since removed roles (#288) and introduced MachineProvider and cloud agents (#309). So everything except wsOrigin.ts, the Docker prompt text and the model-adopt fix is port-adapt, not cherry-pick.

forks.overview: A renamed fork run as a live, self-hosting cubefarm office (CEO branded 'ZetaSoft', on a Linux machine) whose own agents built most of its commits through swarm/issue-N branches, QA rounds and squash merges. Active 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-07: 109 commits ahead of upstream main (about 19.9k insertions over 243 files), 8 behind (it lacks upstream #305 to #311: --host, cloud agents on Upstash Box, the fridge, the preview gateway, local models, the freeze fixes). About half the work is 3D game and world content: penalty shoot-out, smoke breaks, revolving door and grounds, touch controls and phone HUD. The rest is real pipeline work: a CEO code-review merge gate, handling of Actions jobs blocked by billing, per-CLI session limits, Claude-only usage brakes, custom OpenAI-compatible providers, a vision 'look' MCP tool, OpenCode 2 compatibility, Bun installs, chat attachments and desk-work preservation.
forks.license_note: LICENSE is byte-identical to upstream (blob 3b244d0, MIT); no license change. It adds AGENTS.md as a git symlink to CLAUDE.md, and CLAUDE.md's SAFETY section is rewritten for the fork owner's local Linux paths.

features.title: Per-floor CEO code review as a merge gate (approve_pull / request_changes)
features.description: New per-floor switch. When QA passes a PR on such a floor, the office queues a 'code-review' CEO job: it writes the PR diff (gh pr diff, capped at 400 KB) to a file under the CEO folder and prompts the CEO with QA's summary, the linked issue body and the diff path. Two new zod-validated CEO tools act only on that job's PR and only while its head is still the QA-passed SHA. approve_pull posts a review comment and sets QaRecord.ceoApprovedSha; the pure mergeStep waits for it ('waiting for the CEO's code review') before merging. request_changes posts the note and sends the PR back to a developer through sendBackToDev with allowPassed. Stale reviews (new commits, or the switch turned off) are dropped. A review that ends with no verdict posts one office message. Turning the switch on queues reviews for already-passed PRs. Includes the PR card note and the console toggle, plus a demo script in which the demo CEO approves.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream 157efde has no approve_pull, ceoApprovedSha or prDiff. Upstream's 'ceoReview' (client/src/api.ts:129, POST /api/ceo/review) is the CEO's company-review job, a different feature, and it collides with the fork's repo.ceoReview setting name.
features.rfc_relation: spec/review + merge gate (independent review after QA, before merge)
features.rationale: The fork's work closest to the plan -> spec -> independent review -> approval -> merge vision. The design is clean: the decision stays in pure mergeStep, the tools are guarded by job, PR and SHA, and there are a demo fake, codeReview.test.ts and mergeGate tests. 8d67bf6, 60e7f73 and d885e43 apply cleanly to upstream; c46b251 and a9fc070 conflict in ceo.ts and swarm.ts. When porting, rename the setting to avoid the upstream ceoReview clash. Also generalize the reviewer beyond 'the CEO on Claude' (any agent or model, which fits model routing), and store the verdict as an artifact rather than only a SHA field.
features.risks: Posts PR comments through gh. Adds one CEO (Claude) session per passed PR, a cost increase. Diffs over 400 KB are reviewed truncated.

features.title: Don't burn fix rounds on GitHub Actions jobs that never started (billing or spending limit)
features.description: github.ts gains neverStartedJobs/jobNeverStarted, which read the check-run annotations and the job record (no steps, no runner) through gh api. mergeStep gets a 'rerun-blocked' step and a 'blocked' wait: when every failed check is a never-started job, it re-runs them every 30 minutes instead of sending the PR back to a developer, and mergeFixes never grows. The answer is cached per head commit and job. One office message is posted per floor per block. QA's checks line marks those checks so QA doesn't fail the PR for them. The demo fakes nothing as blocked.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream mergeGate.ts has no rerun-blocked step. git grep for neverStarted and 'spending limit' finds nothing in 157efde.
features.rationale: A real failure mode on private repos with Actions budgets: agents waste fix rounds and reach needs-human for nothing. Self-contained, with a pure core and tests (actionsBilling.test.ts, github.test.ts, mergeGate.test.ts). The patch conflicts with upstream in mergeGate.ts and swarm.ts only because the fork's code-review fields are stacked under it; port it after or alongside the code-review gate.
features.risks: Adds two gh api calls per failed job id when checks fail (rate-limit exposure on big offices).

features.title: Re-QA a passed PR on hand-merge floors when its branch gets new commits
features.description: On floors with auto-merge off, a QA-passed PR whose swarm branch got a new commit stayed 'passed' on the old commit forever, because the head-moved requeue only existed in the auto-merge path. A pure movedSincePass() in mergeGate.ts now selects those records, and syncRepo requeues them for a fresh QA round.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no movedSincePass. Upstream swarm.ts checks passedSha only in the auto-merge path (advanceMerge, line ~1625) and in the sync at line 4590.
features.rfc_relation: approvals / merge gate integrity (an approval must bind to the tested commit)
features.rationale: Correctness of the QA gate when a human merges: otherwise the manager can merge untested commits shown as 'passed'. Small (80 lines), with a pure helper and tests. The patch fails to apply cleanly in swarm.ts only around nearby lines.

features.title: Kanban: a merged Ready card goes straight to Merged (never flickers back to In QA)
features.description: closeCleanup.ts gains settledPulls, which brings a floor's OPEN pulls in step with learned CLOSED or MERGED states (backfilling mergedAt); learnPull and settleLearned use it. dropRecord flushes the outbox before qaRemoved. The demo's listPulls now returns copies: shared mutable objects had masked the bug in demo mode.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream closeCleanup.ts has no settledPulls. Upstream demo listPulls still returns the store's own objects.
features.rationale: A small, tested fix for a visible board glitch, plus a demo-parity bug (a shared-reference mask) that would also hide other bugs from e2e.

features.title: Read '## Blocked by' dependency lists; release all held issues of a floor
features.description: shared/issues.ts blockers() now also reads a 'Depends on'/'Blocked by' heading (markdown heading, bold, or 'Blocked by:' line) followed by '- #N' / '1. #N' / checkbox list items. setDependsOn() rewrites that form away. Adds POST /api/repos/:repo/release-held, Swarm.releaseHeld(), and a 'Release N held issues' button on the console's issues tab.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream shared/issues.ts already parses inline 'Depends on #3' / 'Blocked by #4, #5' (shared/issues.test.ts:11-63) but not heading-plus-list blocks. There is no release-held route in upstream index.ts.
features.rationale: The patch applies cleanly to upstream. Issue templates and planners (including the user's own docs and other AI tools) often write dependency lists as headings, so without this the scheduler starts blocked work. Tested (issues.test.ts, releaseHeld.test.ts).

features.title: A chat with a developer whose fix already ended no longer counts as a fix round
features.description: A manager chat resumes the developer's finished fix session, so its end lands in onFixFinished. It is now treated as the fix only while the QA record still waits on that developer (status 'fixing' with this developer as fixer). Otherwise there is no second QA round and no failed-session strike.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream onFixFinished (swarm.ts:3590) has no such guard. fixChat.test.ts does not exist upstream.
features.rationale: Applies cleanly. Prevents spurious QA rounds and strikes when the manager talks to agents, which a human-in-the-loop factory does constantly.

features.title: Save a desk's unfinished work (including new untracked files) before the desk is reused
features.description: saveLeftovers now includes new, untracked, non-ignored files (git add -N in chunks of 100 to stay under Windows' command-line cap, then git diff HEAD --binary). A new saveBeforeReuse runs in setUpWorktree before reuseDesk, skips qa/pr-* desks, clears a stale index.lock, and skips commits that were squash-merged (a merge-tree check with a fallback for old git). A failed save leaves a note and never blocks reuse.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream workspace.ts uses 'status --porcelain --untracked-files=no' (lines 154, 540) and has no saveBeforeReuse.
features.rationale: Prevents silent loss of agents' work (new files were dropped). Applies cleanly to upstream, has extensive workspace tests including Windows command-line chunking, and follows the Windows-first conventions. Covers local machines only; upstream's Box machines would need their own equivalent.

features.title: Resume a session only in the CLI that made it; track the developer session's CLI on QA records
features.description: A pure resumeChoice() in clis.ts: live follow-ups stay with the session's CLI. Every other start (task, QA, fix) runs on the agent's current CLI and drops a session made by a different or unknown CLI, with a log line. QaRecord gets devSessionCli. A CEO chat keeps resuming its own Claude session.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has sessionCli (swarm.ts:159) and a simpler rule in sessionRuntime (it switches to the session's CLI in the terminal runtime). It has no resumeChoice and no devSessionCli.
features.rfc_relation: model routing (switching an agent's CLI or model mid-pipeline)
features.rationale: Needed once agents switch CLIs or providers, which the routing vision assumes. The sessionRuntime hunk conflicts directly with upstream's cloud-agent changes (a.host === 'box' forcing the terminal runtime), so port the pure rule and rewire it by hand.

features.title: Watchdog judges a working agent by the CLI it is running now
features.description: watchdog.ts and swarm.ts use the running session's CLI (agentRt.cli) instead of the agent's last saved session CLI when deciding the sign-of-life rules, so a Codex or OpenCode session isn't judged by Claude's hook cadence.
features.already_upstream_evidence: The patch applies cleanly to upstream 157efde, so upstream's watchdog lines are unchanged from the merge base.
features.rationale: A tiny, clean fix for mixed-CLI offices that prevents false stall detection.

features.title: Session limits per coding agent (and per custom provider) instead of one office-wide cap
features.description: settings.sessionLimit becomes sessionLimits: Partial<Record<CliId, number>>, migrated from the old value. slotsFull() becomes cliFull(cli), checked against the CLI each session will actually run (pure sessionCli and nextCli rules; busy sessions count against their running CLI). The scheduler filters out agents whose CLI is full, so a full Claude never blocks a free OpenCode agent. The snapshot and company_status report sessionsRunning per CLI, the CEO prompt lists each cap, and the Settings tab shows one input per CLI. HUD, phone and lobby show per-CLI counts.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream swarm.ts still has a single settings.sessionLimit (lines 493, 1328, 2640, 3706). There is no sessionLimits.
features.rfc_relation: cost telemetry + model routing (per-provider concurrency budgets)
features.rationale: Core to running a mixed fleet (subscriptions, API keys, local models) without one provider starving the others. It touches swarm.ts, pacing.ts, ceo.ts and 5 UI files, conflicts heavily with upstream cloud agents, and is typed on the fork's CliId widening. Port together with the Claude-only brakes and decide how cloud (Box) agents count.

features.title: Usage brakes and pacing hold only Claude sessions; other coding agents carry on
features.description: pacing.ts: mayStart takes a 'uses Claude' flag and a runningClaude count, and limitExempt(limited, usedClaude) decides when a failure is the usage limit's fault. In the SDK runtime everything counts as Claude. The scheduler picks only agents the brake allows, so a held Claude desk no longer blocks Codex or OpenCode desks.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream pacing.ts mayStart(kind, {running, pacingSessions}) has no per-CLI notion. git grep for usesClaude returns nothing at 157efde.
features.rationale: Without this a Claude 5-hour limit stalls the whole factory even when other providers are idle. Pure, tested logic, but woven through swarm.ts scheduling that upstream changed. Port it as one unit with per-cli-session-limits.

features.title: Live Claude 5-hour and weekly usage gauges (not just the 90% warning)
features.description: shared/usage.ts parses the status line's rate_limits into readings. cliRunner and agentRunner report them through a new usageReading callback. Swarm keeps the latest five_hour and seven_day readings, and pacing.usageView exposes UsageView.limits. The console usage card and the lobby screen draw one gauge per limit. The demo grows plausible readings per session.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream cliRunner.ts onStatus (lines ~625-640) already reads rate_limits.used_percentage, but only to fire a warning at >= USAGE_WARN_PCT. It has no continuous readings or gauges.

features.title: OpenCode 2 compatibility: folder plugin, --standalone, model via config, CLI exit errors surfaced

Each session runs with --standalone (its own server, config and plugin env). The model goes in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT.model, since OpenCode 2.1.3 has no --model flag.
