forks.overview: A one-author fork (Paulo Lopes, with Claude as co-author) that replaces cubefarm's 3D office with a role-based 2D web dashboard. The roles are CEO, Developer, Reviewer, Metrics and Settings. The server, shared/ and the REST/WS contract are left untouched. All 65 commits landed in a 2-day burst (2026-11-05/06) through an internal PR flow (#1-#49), followed by a documented plan (docs/plan-2d-dashboard.md). main is 65 ahead and 0 behind upstream 157efde: 8.7k lines added and about 88k deleted (world/, photo/, three.js deps, bench, 3D e2e). Fork commit 78a4d42 is the best import point. At that commit the full dashboard exists while the 3D office is still there (dashboard is the default, 3D via ?office=3d). Later commits delete the 3D office.
forks.license_note: Still MIT with Leon van Zyl's notice kept. One line was added: 'Copyright (c) 2026 Paulo Lopes'. Importing substantial dashboard code means carrying that copyright line into our LICENSE. No other licensing change.

features.title: Decouple non-3D client code from world/ (effects registry, sfx core/spatial split, pure helpers, guard test)
features.description: Phase 0 of the fork's plan, with no visible behaviour change. Pure helpers move out of world/: toolVerb.ts, cards.ts (with a geometry-free findCard replacing locateCard), qaRecord.ts and merges.ts. A typed channel registry (client/src/effects.ts, with sticky channels for late-loading lazy chunks) carries merge/gong/reward/presence/replay effects, so store.ts and replay.ts no longer import world/. sfx.ts is split into a 2D core and a 3D-only sfxSpatial.ts, and music ducking becomes a hook. TerminalView, SetupWizard and AgentSettings take onFollow/lookEditor/careerCard/onFinish as optional props. LookEditor.tsx and TeamStats.tsx are split out, and Phone.tsx gets a 3D-only Phone3D. noWorldImports.test.ts statically checks, directly and transitively, that pocket/dashboard code never reaches world/, photo/, three or @react-three.

The fork main descends from 157efde (behind 0), so every commit is new.
features.rfc_relation: none (UI architecture enabler for any non-3D control surface)
features.rationale: This is the prerequisite for every dashboard feature below. It also makes store.ts testable without the 3D graph, and the guard test keeps a light 2D or headless chunk light. It applies cleanly on 157efde (it descends from it). The medium risk comes from moving code out of upstream hot files: store.ts had 52 upstream commits in the last month and sfx.ts 25. Every later upstream sync, and any other fork's import touching those files, will need manual merging.
features.risks: None external. Medium ongoing merge cost against upstream's store.ts/sfx.ts churn.

It shows labels at 1024px and up, icons only at 760-1024px, and becomes pocket's bottom tab bar below that. Also included: a top bar with a floor picker and the usage/update banners, a non-modal right drawer (Esc, dialogFocus), the setup wizard on a fresh office, and an ActivityFeed from ticker events. route.ts (pure) parses and formats #/ceo, #/dev/:floor(/terminals), #/review/:floor/:pr, #/metrics and #/settings/:tab, and maps notification ?tab= links. badges.ts computes per-role counts (approvals plus unread for CEO, errors for Developer, needs-you plus ready for Reviewer, alarms plus doctor findings for Metrics). watch.ts dashboardWatch with dashboard/visible.ts tells the server exactly which agents' terminal lines are on screen; this is client-only and the server contract is unchanged. mode.ts makes the dashboard the default and the 3D office opt-in (?office=3d or a button, remembered per device).

forks.overview: A fork run as its own live office (agent branches swarm/issue-N-karen, -brendan, -holmes, -tester-50) that worked through a planned 'safety integration' epic: a local Host/Origin request boundary, a fail-closed merge gate, workspace/commit preservation, a global scheduler pause, CEO-reserving session slots, crash recovery, issue-filing idempotency and enforced git rules, plus its own voice/hands-free stack. The work sits on two separate lines. main is based on upstream 31e7ce0 (2026-10-02, 134 commits behind) and has most stories. codex/integrate-safety-upstream (and swarm/issue-8-karen) was rebased onto current upstream 157efde and has only S1 (request boundary), S2.1-S2.3 (merge gate), S4.1 (pure slot policy, not wired), S5.1 (preservation) and docs. The fork's own approval record (docs/safety-integration-approval.md, S6.3) is RED because no single commit has all the stories. Active until 2026-11-12.
forks.license_note: LICENSE unchanged versus upstream MIT on both lines, and package.json has no fork-side changes. The commits carry Claude Haiku, Cursor Agent and Codex co-author trailers and a personal author email (data only, not a licensing issue).

features.title: Fail-closed Host/Origin/Sec-Fetch request boundary for HTTP, /ws and /ws/term (CSRF and DNS-rebinding defence)
features.description: Pure policy server/requestBoundary.ts (officeRequest). It accepts only an exact Host of localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1] with the bound port (plus the Vite port in dev), rejects duplicate or malformed headers (checks rawHeaders), absolute-form targets and Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, and requires Origin on unsafe methods and websocket upgrades. index.ts runs it as the first middleware and in server.on('upgrade') before routing. Agent callbacks POST /api/hooks|mcp/:token may omit Origin only when cliRunner.hasCliRoute confirms a live token, checked before the JSON body is parsed (64 MB limit). Look-alike callback paths get 403. Playwright sends an Origin header.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/index.ts has no Host/Origin/Sec-Fetch check (grep for req.headers.host/origin finds only previewGateway's sec-fetch use). Upstream f32ce7d added --host/SWARM_HOST, and docs/pocket.md says it 'has no sign-in'. The branch's merge-base is 157efde, so the whole diff is new.
features.rfc_relation: security (local API exposure of an unsandboxed agent runner)
features.rationale: This is the most important missing protection upstream. Any web page the manager visits can POST to localhost:4317 and start unsandboxed agents. The policy is pure, well tested (unit, integration and e2e) and applies directly to current upstream. It must be adapted first: the hard-coded loopback allowlist breaks upstream's --host LAN/Tailscale mode, pocket mode and the preview gateway for other devices. Allow the configured SWARM_HOST/network names, and add a token or pairing step whenever HOST is not loopback.
features.risks: Breaking change for --host and phone users if imported as is. Its docs say 'never bind 0.0.0.0', which contradicts upstream's feature. index.ts changes often upstream. Exporting `server` from index.ts is a side change.

features.title: Per-run session token on /api and websockets plus simple Host/Origin allowlist (fork main variant)
features.description: A random 32-byte token is created at startup. GET /api/session returns it without authentication, the client sends it as X-Session-Token on REST calls and ?token= on websockets, and a string-equality Host/Origin check limits access to localhost/127.0.0.1:PORT. #86 moved it into server/requestBoundary.ts createRequestBoundary.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no /api/session route and no token on /ws (client/src/net.ts opens /ws without a token).
features.rationale: The protection really comes from the Host/Origin check. The token adds little because /api/session hands it to any request that passes that check. A missing Origin is accepted, and the Vite proxy rewrite (separate entry) defeats the check in dev. The codex boundary is strictly better. Keep only the idea of a token or pairing code for non-loopback --host mode.
features.risks: Written against the 134-behind base: client api.ts, net.ts and LiveTerminal changes conflict. Tokens in websocket query strings end up in logs.

features.title: Fail-closed merge gate: one fresh PR detail, QA-passed exact SHA, review/draft/checks/mergeState, same path for manual and auto merges
features.description: github.ts prDetails returns isDraft, reviewDecision and a checks rollup from one gh pr view, and checksOf treats neutral/skipped-only rollups as 'none' rather than passing. mergeGate.ts adds a pure mergeGate(rec, pr) with typed refusals (not-passed, no-passed-sha, head-moved, not-open, draft, checks-not-passing, changes-requested, merge-state) and removes the legacy line that set a missing passedSha to the head. swarm.ts gatedMerge() is used by both the manager's merge button and auto-merge. It merges with --match-head-commit at QA's passed SHA, and a refused auto-merge re-queues QA. The manual merge button returns 409 unless QA passed the current head. main also has S2.5, a negative-path test matrix asserting merge is called zero times.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream mergeGate.ts mergeStep waits on drafts and merges rec.passedSha ?? headSha, but line 47 still sets a missing passedSha to the head. listPulls fetches reviewDecision, but mergeStep never checks it. Upstream Swarm.mergePull (swarm.ts:1921-1924) calls backend.mergePull with no gate and no SHA pin.
features.rationale: This is the core of the RFC's merge gate: merge only the exact SHA that was reviewed and approved, and refuse on missing data. It is pure, well tested and already on current upstream. Two policy choices need adapting. checks !== 'passing' refuses repos with no CI forever (upstream merges on 'none'), and mergeState must be exactly CLEAN (refusing UNSTABLE/HAS_HOOKS). Also, making the manager's button QA-only removes the human override, so add an explicit override or approval path.
features.risks: Behaviour change: no-CI floors would never merge, and the manual merge override disappears. swarm.ts advanceMerge and mergePull are hot spots upstream.

features.title: Updating a PR branch with the base sends it back to QA instead of moving passedSha to the untested head
features.description: After advanceMerge calls GitHub's update-branch (base merged into the PR), retestPatch() sets the QA record to queued with passedSha null, instead of upstream's fetch-new-head-and-set-passedSha. The merged result must therefore pass QA again.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream swarm.ts:1623-1625 runs updateBranch, then prDetails, then setQa({ passedSha: details.headSha }). The never-tested merge commit is treated as QA-passed.
features.rationale: A small, real integrity fix: otherwise the office merges a SHA that QA never saw. Take it as a few lines plus a test, and make it configurable (re-QA, or trust CI on base-only merges). On busy repos every base move would otherwise trigger another QA round.
features.risks: Extra QA rounds and agent cost on repos whose base moves often.

features.title: Never lose desk work: refuse to reset dirty worktrees, pin unpushed commits to refs/cubefarm-recovery before deleting
features.description: workspace.ts adds preserveCommit, which writes a verified, never-overwritten ref under refs/cubefarm-recovery/<label>/<stamp>-<sha>-<rand> (or pushes it into the floor checkout) when a commit is on no remote branch. guardWorktree refuses (PreservationError) if a worktree has any change, including untracked files, or is not its own worktree. Both run before setUpWorktree's -B, removeDesk, sweepDesks, the branch -D batches, sweepMachine and removeMachine. A branch that cannot be preserved is skipped and logged.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream workspace.ts saveLeftovers (line 537) writes a patch of leftovers before sweeps and machine removal, but deletes branches with plain branch -D batches and does not pin unpushed commits. There is no recovery-ref namespace.
features.rationale: Losing an agent's unpushed commits is a real failure mode in a factory with many desks. Recovery refs are cheap, git-native and reviewable. Adapt it rather than taking it whole: throwing on dirty desks in setUpWorktree can stall an agent's next task until someone cleans up by hand (upstream's patch approach does not block), recovery refs need pruning or a UI, and Upstash Box machines (boxMachines.ts) are not covered.
features.risks: Stalled desks, refs that pile up without limit, extra git calls per sweep on floors with hundreds of branches. workspace.ts changes heavily upstream.

features.title: Global persisted 'Pause scheduling' kill switch (SWARM_START_PAUSED, rechecked after async preparation)
features.description: settings.schedulerPaused (persisted). SWARM_START_PAUSED=1 can only force it on. While paused nothing autonomous starts: auto-assign, QA, fixes, CEO jobs, restart recovery, nudges and auto-merge all hold. The pause is checked again after desk preparation (holdForPause clears the task but keeps the desk) and just before merge. There is a toggle in Manager console > Settings, plus ManagerConsole.test.tsx and a 353-line schedulerPause.test.ts.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has per-floor autoAssign/autoMerge toggles (shared/types.ts:68-69) and a usage-limit pausedUntil (swarm.ts:3795), but no global manager pause and no SWARM_START_PAUSED.
features.rationale: A global halt is a basic control for a factory that runs many agents and multiple repos. The design (re-check after every await, never kill running sessions) is sound. The code is written against a swarm.ts that is 134 commits old, so re-implement it on upstream's scheduler using the fork's tests as the specification.
features.risks: Touches many scheduler paths in swarm.ts. Missing one launch path would silently ignore the pause.

features.title: Reserve session slots synchronously before preparing, and keep one slot for an idle CEO
features.description: server/sessionSlots.ts mayReserveSlot (pure, fails closed). Swarm.withSlot reserves the slot before async desk preparation and releases it however the launch ends; a failed preparation becomes an error and does not hold the slot. Workers can use at most sessionLimit-1 slots while the CEO is idle. The wiring (S4.2) is only on main. On the codex line the pure module and its test are dead code.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has settings.sessionLimit and slotsFull() (swarm.ts:1327-1330). It counts only BUSY statuses, does not reserve a slot during preparation and keeps no slot for the CEO.
features.rationale: Fixes a real race: concurrent starts during preparation can exceed the limit, and the CEO can be crowded out. The pure policy can be cherry-picked. The wiring has to be redone on upstream's launch paths, including cloud Box agents.
features.risks: Changes when work starts. A missed release path would leak slots.

features.title: Crash recovery that checks remote PR state before resuming a writer, with a crash-matrix test suite and runbook
features.description: After a restart, recover() reads the agent's PR (saved number, then prForBranch, then prDetails) before replaying a session. Open PRs go to QA. Ambiguous cases (failed read, a terminal PR on a reused issue branch, no saved PR identity) hold the task with a log line. Closed or merged fix PRs are reconciled without replay, and their QA record is kept in the log. Adds server/crashRecovery.test.ts (539 lines, fixtures/crashOffice.ts) and docs/crash-recovery.md.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has since added server/reconcile.ts (workState, reconcileStep: clear/reattach/resume/requeue), restartRecovery.ts (resumesAfterRestart, followKeptCli), and commits 5e27150 'resume the right task after a restart' and 10a9505 'Re-queue QA a restart left in testing'.
features.rationale: Upstream solved most of this differently, with a terminal keeper and reconcile.ts. The useful parts are the crash-matrix scenarios and the rule that a failed read means uncertainty, not failure. Port those as tests against upstream's reconcile.ts, not the code.
features.risks: The code targets an old recover(), and the runbook mentions npm run demo with custom ports. Do not import as is.

features.title: Durable, idempotent issue filing (operation log plus hidden body marker, reconciled after lost acknowledgements)
features.description: state.issueOperations records key, fingerprint, marker and status (ready, attempting, complete, unresolved). The state is written before the GitHub call. On retry, findIssueByMarker paginates every issue (state=all, excluding PRs) looking for an <!-- cubefarm-operation: sha --> marker in the body. The REST body accepts idempotencyKey. The CEO's file_issue tool now requires an idempotency_key. There is a demo fake.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream ceo.ts and swarm.ts have no idempotency or marker logic. The CEO is only told in its prompt not to duplicate issues (ceo.ts:283).
features.rationale: Exactly-once external writes matter for an artifact-driven factory, but this version is heavy. It paginates all issues on each reconcile (slow on large repos, uses rate limit), the operation log grows without limit, every CEO call pays for a key, and every issue body gets a marker comment. Reuse the pattern in a lighter form for a provider-agnostic task store.
features.risks: GitHub rate limits, state.json growth, CEO tool schema change (prompt cost).

features.title: Quarantine state-file records with unknown roles or statuses instead of coercing them
features.description: quarantineDiagnostics() keeps agents or QA records whose role/status this version does not know, never schedules them, and logs a warning on the agent.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No quarantine logic upstream. Upstream changed AgentRole to 'agent' | 'ceo' (shared/types.ts:148).
features.rationale: The fork's hard-coded ROLES ['dev','qa','ceo'] would quarantine every agent in an upstream state file. Useful only as an idea for schema-versioned state.
features.risks: Imported as is, it would freeze all upstream agents.

features.title: Enforced agent git rules: PreToolUse denials, OpenCode permission map, Codex hook decisions, per-worktree pre-push hook
features.description: server/gitSafety.ts denies, by regex and tokenised shell parsing, force-push, push to main/master/default, remote branch deletion, --no-verify, gh pr merge, merges through gh api, and for QA any commit, push, gh write or file edit. agentRunner canUseTool and cliRunner PreToolUse return deny. clis.ts sets OpenCode permission.bash and makes the Codex hook script return the office's decision. installAgentGitHooks sets core.hooksPath per worktree to a cubefarm pre-push hook that refuses the default branch, deletions and non-fast-forwards.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream cliRunner always answers PreToolUse with allow. CLAUDE.md SAFETY says workflow rules 'live in their prompts and instructions, not in enforcement: don't add hooks, permission rules or sandboxes that refuse tool calls.'
features.rationale: Enforced policy fits a governed factory, but it reverses an explicit upstream design rule, so the user must decide. Quality is weak: PRs #84 and #85 merged two overlapping implementations (blockedCommand and checkAgentShellCommand), regex shell parsing is easy to get around, and core.hooksPath silently disables the target repo's own hooks (husky/lefthook) in agent worktrees. Rebuild it as one opt-in 'enforced rules' setting that chains existing hooks, and rely on GitHub branch protection as the real control.
features.risks: Breaks repos that rely on their own git hooks. False denials can stall agents. Turns on extensions.worktreeConfig in the shared clone. Contradicts upstream CLAUDE.md.

features.title: Auto-merge off by default for new and loaded floors
features.description: New floors get autoMerge false, and loaded floors without the field default to false (upstream defaults true). QA-passed PRs then wait for the manager's merge.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream swarm.ts:689 has r.autoMerge ?? true, and line 1421 sets autoMerge: true for new floors.
features.rationale: Belongs in the RFC's configurable workflow (a per-floor approval step) rather than a hard-coded default flip. Changing ?? true to ?? false on load silently changes behaviour for existing offices.
features.risks: Silent behaviour change for existing users' floors.

features.title: Vite dev proxy rewrites Host/Origin to the server port
features.description: vite.config.ts proxies /api and /ws to 127.0.0.1 with changeOrigin and forces Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<serverPort>, so the fork-main origin check passes in dev.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream vite.config.ts proxies to localhost with no header rewrites. Upstream has no origin check that would need it.
features.rationale: Rewriting Origin at the proxy defeats the origin check in dev: any page that reaches Vite gets a trusted Origin. The codex boundary allows the Vite client port instead, which is the correct approach.
features.risks: Hides cross-origin requests in dev.

features.title: Explain why the mic and hands-free cannot work (insecure HTTP page, pending permission prompt) and add a Mic check panel
features.description: micCaps gains secure (window.isSecureContext). cantListen and micErrorLine return a one-line explanation (use localhost or HTTPS via Tailscale Serve) on insecure pages. A mic that never starts now reports 'not-allowed' instead of a silent stop. MicButton shows 'Waiting for the browser's microphone prompt' after 2 s. VoiceSettings adds a Mic check row (secure, recognition, recorder, permission, Test mic button). Includes micText tests and e2e/mic.spec cases.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream client/src/ui/micText.ts, mic.ts and MicButton.tsx have no isSecureContext or 'secure' handling (grep empty). The branch is based on 157efde.
features.rationale: Small, tested and already on current upstream. It matters now because upstream's --host makes LAN HTTP access common, and browsers block the mic there. Fix the 'on this Mac' wording before importing (the office is Windows-first).
features.risks: Copy wording only. The Codex-generated message references docs/pocket.md, which should be checked.

features.title: Fork's own browser speech recognition, synthesis and hands-free CEO conversation
features.description: MicButton, mic.ts, handsFree.ts, voiceReply.ts, VoiceSettings, Phone integration, ceoVoiceProvider/handsFreeModeEnabled settings, and e2e/mic.spec.ts with real hands-free scenarios, written on the old base because 'the voice stack is not on main'.

features.rationale: An independent reimplementation of a feature upstream already ships in a fuller form. Nothing to import beyond the diagnostics entry above.

features.title: Before/after visual evidence guide for UI PRs
features.description: docs/visual-evidence.md is a checklist: same viewport and state, before revision versus tested head SHA, redact private data, pass/fail/skipped labels. Linked from CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and how-it-works.md. It mentions the external vercel-labs/before-and-after tool.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream QA already posts screenshots through the swarm-qa-evidence branch (github.ts:307 EVIDENCE_BRANCH), and PR theatre (bfa77c9) shows a PR side by side with main. There is no written before/after checklist.
features.rationale: The valuable version is automatic: QA captures base and head at the same viewport (PR theatre's compare mode already runs both) and attaches the pair as a review artifact. A human checklist alone adds little.
features.risks: References an external project. The CLAUDE.md change adds prompt text agents pay for in every session.

features.title: docs/local-safety.md threat model (browser CSRF/rebinding, PR authors untrusted, least privilege, pause, slot cap)
features.description: A clear in-scope/out-of-scope threat model for an unsandboxed agent runner, with least-privilege advice for gh tokens and branch protection, and descriptions of the pause and session cap.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream docs/ has agents, cloud, how-it-works, pocket and voice only.
features.rationale: A useful basis for the factory's security doc. It must be rewritten: it says 'never bind 0.0.0.0, no tunnel, no reverse proxy', which contradicts upstream --host and Tailscale pocket mode, and it describes a pause and slot cap that are not wired on that branch.
features.risks: Doc and code drift as published.

features.title: Ledger test fixture avoids the Sydney daylight-saving gap
features.description: server/ledger.test.ts builds local times in July instead of October, so 02:00 on 4 October exists in every timezone. The test fails in Australia/Sydney.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/ledger.test.ts:9 still uses new Date(2026, 9, day, h, m).
features.rationale: A one-line, harmless timezone fix for a flaky test.

features.title: Planned epic run by the office itself: S-numbered stories with owned files, base SHA contract, GREEN = test + code review + security on one assembled SHA
features.description: docs/safety-integration-plan.md (epics, dependency graph, per-story files it owns, 'Base: <branch> @ <sha>' contract), docs/baseline-d3b47c6.md, issue records for S0.2, S6.2 and S6.3 (docs/safety-integration-approval.md: RED, no assembled SHA), and docs/issue-37-readiness.md. Process artifacts only.

features.rationale: A live example of the target workflow (plan, stories, independent reviews, approval on an assembled SHA) done by hand through issues and docs. It also shows what fails without tooling: the work split across two heads and was never assembled. Use it as requirements input, not code.

features.title: CI e2e job: longer timeout, cache restore-keys, Playwright install retry

features.title: swarm-qa-evidence orphan branch (runtime QA screenshots)
features.description: 22 commits of PNG screenshots for the fork's own PRs (pr-28 through pr-83) plus a README, written by the office's QA evidence uploader.
features.already_upstream_evidence: The mechanism is upstream (server/github.ts:307 EVIDENCE_BRANCH = 'swarm-qa-evidence'). The content is the fork's runtime data.

features.title: WIP snapshot 'Preserve local safety and scheduling changes' (stateCompat, early pause/slots/boundary)
features.description: A single commit on d3b47c6 dumping an early working tree: shared/stateCompat.ts maps non-qa/ceo roles to 'dev', plus early drafts of the boundary, pause, slots and merge gate (swarm.ts net -1700 lines against its base).

method_notes: Partial clone (blob:none) of localloop-pro/cubefarm with upstream main fetched. I ran no npm, node or fork code. I checked all 34 non-default branches plus main. They form two lines: (a) main and its swarm/issue-14..82 descendants on upstream 31e7ce0 (134 behind), and (b) codex/integrate-safety-upstream and swarm/issue-8-karen (merge-base = 157efde), plus codex/issue-2/3/9, swarm/issue-4/5/7/8/9/10/11 and swarm/docs-visual-evidence on d3b47c6 (8 behind). None of the swarm/issue-N branches is a copy of an upstream PR. All are fork-internal PRs, and most were squash-merged into fork main; I matched single unique commits to main's squash titles (for example ae464a7 to 1e27b69, 78f3ff6 to 4ef8175, a51410e to b201d5c, c313813 to 44ac92f). For line (b), the diff against upstream/main is by definition not upstream. For fork main, reverse-apply checks are meaningless at 134 behind, so I judged 'already upstream' by reading and grepping the same concerns in the upstream checkout (index.ts, mergeGate.ts, swarm.ts mergePull/updateBranch, workspace.ts saveLeftovers, reconcile.ts/restartRecovery.ts, voice files, ci.yml, ledger.test.ts). I read the main code diffs in full (swarm.ts, index.ts, requestBoundary both variants, mergeGate, github, workspace, gitSafety and its runner wiring, sessionSlots, issue idempotency, mic diagnostics, vite config) and skimmed docs. Not read line by line: crashRecovery.test.ts (539 lines), schedulerPause.test.ts (353), sessionSlots.integration.test.ts, e2e/mic.spec.ts (420), the fork's voice stack client files (classified as superseded by file size and structure against upstream), and the evidence PNGs. One git grep across a tree started fetching blobs lazily and I stopped it; afterwards I used single-file git show. Line counts are approximate.

forks.overview: A production fork run by one consultant (BC Consulting branding, an 'openRTSM' floor in its docs) that turns cubefarm into a governed, mostly autonomous office: technical problems are handled by the office, and only business decisions reach the manager, as structured decision briefs answered in a Decision room, with merge holds, risk-based routine-only auto-merge, a decision clock, a per-floor 'floor lead' agent with an undoable board log, and CEO email via Microsoft Graph. Very active: 17 PRs from 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-10, all squash-merged into its main, plus one unmerged branch (settings-logout). Based on upstream d3b47c6, only 8 commits behind upstream 157efde, but about 11.7k lines added (swarm.ts grows by ~1950 lines); a full merge conflicts in 10 files, mostly additive collisions with upstream's cloud-agents (Upstash Box) PR.
forks.license_note: LICENSE blob identical to upstream (MIT, 3b244d0). No license change. The reskin adds an Adobe Typekit kit (use.typekit.net/ylc4ofo.css) and BC Consulting logos/icons, which are the fork owner's licensed fonts and brand assets and must not be imported.

features.title: Per-PR merge holds: floor hold paths (gitignore-style globs) and the swarm:hold label keep a QA-passed PR from auto-merging; held PRs stay current
features.description: Adds holdPaths per floor (PATCH /api/repos/:repo, console textarea) and the swarm:hold label. In the auto-merge loop, a passed PR whose changed files (gh api pulls/N/files, cached per head SHA) match a pattern, or that carries the label, is marked heldFor and never merged; the manager gets one phone message/notification naming the file or label; the card shows 'held for you'. Follow-up fix: held PRs still take every merge step except the merge itself (conflicts go back to a developer, branch kept up to date) so it can merge the moment the manager approves. Pure matcher in shared/holds.ts with tests; demo fake prFiles.
features.already_upstream_evidence: grep of upstream main (157efde) server/ and shared/ for holdPaths, swarm:hold, heldFor, prFiles: no matches. Upstream mergeStep has no hold concept.
features.rationale: Small, pure, well-tested, demo parity, and the exact primitive a human-approval merge gate needs. 32b3ed8 cherry-picks onto upstream 157efde with zero conflicts (verified in a temp worktree); 2698c4c applies cleanly after it. Natural foundation for the factory's configurable merge gate.
features.risks: None external. Adds one gh API call per PR head SHA on floors with hold paths.

features.title: Routine-only auto-merge: PRs touching migrations, auth, secrets, CI/infra, dependencies, or >400 lines are held for the manager
features.description: Floor switch routineOnly (default ON): on top of merge holds, shared/holds.ts notRoutine() classifies a PR's changed files against built-in rule groups (database migrations/schema, sign-in/permissions, secrets/keys, deploys/CI/infra, dependency manifests and lockfiles) and size (additions+deletions > 400) and holds non-routine PRs with a plain-words reason ('not routine: it changes dependencies (package.json)').
features.already_upstream_evidence: No notRoutine/routineOnly or risk classification in upstream server/ or shared/; upstream auto-merge merges every QA-passed swarm/ PR with green checks.
features.rationale: Risk-tiered merge gating is core to a safe factory, and the code is small and pure. Adapt: make the rule groups and the line threshold configurable per project/workflow (the factory's policy config), and default the switch OFF for existing floors instead of silently holding work after upgrade. Depends on merge holds.
features.risks: Behaviour change: loader sets routineOnly ?? true, so existing auto-merge floors would start holding dependency/CI/large PRs after upgrade. Glob heuristics ('auth', '*secret*') will over-match in some repos.

features.title: Decision briefs: one template/parser for business decisions on needs-input issues and held PRs; ADRs for technical choices
features.description: shared/brief.ts defines a '## Decision brief' markdown template (Background, The decision, Options with trade-offs, Recommendation, Risk and mitigation, If no reply by) with a tolerant parser (headings or bold lines), gap checker, renderer, plain-text lines for alerts, and recommendsMerge(). Build/fix prompts gain DECISIONS_RULE: make technical choices yourself and record an ADR in docs/adr/NNNN-*.md; label needs-input / swarm:hold only for business decisions, with the brief in the body. The CEO gets a write_brief office tool (zod) to post a missing brief; reviews list decisions lacking one.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No brief.ts, write_brief, needs-input, or ADR rule in upstream ceo.ts/prompts.ts (grep for write_brief|needs-input returned nothing).
features.rationale: This is essentially the 'decision artifact' of an artifact-driven workflow: structured, parseable, renderable for phone/email/UI. Port it as a first-class artifact type in the factory's workflow engine rather than as prompt text tied to GitHub labels. The regex-based recommendsMerge() is fragile and should become an explicit enum field in the artifact.
features.risks: Prompt text is paid on every build/fix session (template added to every dev prompt). Parsing natural-language recommendations to decide merges is brittle.

features.title: Decision room: every open decision (needs-input issue, held PR, escalated stuck PR) as a card answered in one tap, with an Ask-the-CEO thread
features.description: New DecisionRoom.tsx overlay (HUD button, pocket-mode tab, Approvals callout, deep links /decisions#owner/repo/N built on the office's public address). Cards show the parsed brief, countdown and thread. Answers (approve recommendation, pick option N, send back with note, close) map via pure server/decisionAnswer.ts to a 'Decision: ...' GitHub comment plus label changes (needs-input -> decided:manager, or close) or the swarm's own merge/send-back/close for PRs. 'Ask' queues a CEO 'decision' job with the card context; the reply lands on the card and as a GitHub comment. Threads/answers persisted in state.json; snapshot + event wiring in store.ts; demo fakes.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No DecisionRoom.tsx, shared/decisions.ts or /decisions route in upstream; upstream only has Approvals for team-change requests.
features.rationale: The single most reusable UX piece for a factory's human-approval step: one inbox of decisions with structured options and an audit comment trail. Port it generalized to 'approval requests' from any workflow stage (spec approval, plan approval, merge approval), not only GitHub issues/PRs. Depends on briefs and merge holds. feat/decision-room (PR #12) was closed unmerged and superseded by feat/decision-room-main (#13).
features.risks: Answers act through the shared GitHub login; the 'Decision:' first-line convention is the only way the office distinguishes manager replies from agents. Adds REST routes that merge/close PRs: must stay behind whatever auth the office has when exposed with --host.

features.title: Decision clock: unanswered decisions get the brief's recommendation applied after decisionTimeoutHours (default 48 h)
features.description: server/decisionClock.ts (pure, tested) tracks first-seen per needs-input issue and held PR in state.json, computes deadline (late briefs get at least 24 h), due-soon flags, detects explicit 'Decision:' replies, and decides the default action: issues get decided:default and are built per the recommendation; held PRs are merged if the brief recommends merging and QA passed with green checks and no conflicts, else sent back with the recommendation as the note. Posts a reversible-explanation comment. Phone alert waits up to 1 h for a brief.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No decisionClock.ts or timeout-based default actions in upstream.
features.rationale: Approval SLAs with escalation are useful, but auto-applying a recommendation (including auto-merging a PR that was held precisely because it touches auth/migrations) defeats a human-approval gate. Port the tracking, deadlines, due-soon reminders and digest flags; make the default action opt-in per workflow with timeout 0 (never) as the default.
features.risks: Safety: default 48 h applies to existing floors on upgrade (decisionTimeoutHours ?? 48), so held PRs can merge without a human. Relies on parsing 'Merge it' from free text.

features.title: Autonomous floors: CEO keeps a minimum ready backlog by filing issues from the brief and roadmap docs (autoPlan, minReady)
features.description: Floor settings autoPlan (default off) and minReady (default 5, max 20). On autoPlan floors the CEO's heartbeat review may file issues (mayFileIssue relaxes upstream's 'only when the manager asked' rule) for the current milestone of docs/roadmap.md / ROADMAP.md, and plans the next milestone when one is done; a review runs even with an unchanged fingerprint while a floor is below minReady, unless the last review filed nothing (roadmap done). Adds Backend.milestones for the digest. Console controls next to Auto-merge.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream ceo.ts enforces NOT_ASKED: file_issue only in plan/chat jobs; no autoPlan/minReady/planReviewDue.
features.rationale: Roadmap-driven backlog replenishment is a key step toward a self-driving factory (plan -> issues). Port as an explicit, opt-in workflow stage that reads a roadmap artifact, with a per-run issue cap and cost budget, rather than as an exception in the CEO's prompt.
features.risks: Token spend: forces CEO reviews while below minReady. Agent-created scope without per-issue human approval (opt-in only).

features.title: Rebuild technical stuck PRs from current main instead of escalating; stuck-PR buttons highlight the office's recommended action
features.description: server/rebuild.ts (pure, tested): when a PR is stuck for a technical reason (conflicts, red checks, failed QA rounds, failed fix sessions, desk setup) and triage is spent, the office closes it with a plain-words comment (branch kept), comments a note for the next developer on the linked issue (or files a new issue when none is linked), re-queues the issue on a fresh branch slug (-r2) with a rebuildNote in the dev prompt. Loop guard MAX_REBUILDS=1: a second stuck rebuild goes to the manager with a 'park it' decision brief (default on timeout: close and park). Business holds still escalate. Retry every 30 min if GitHub refuses. Client: stuckActions.ts orders Kanban/console/pocket buttons by the office's pick with a one-line why.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream CEO triage has close_pull that closes a stuck PR and leaves the issue open 'so it is built again' (swarm.ts triageClosePull, learnPull(..., rebuild=true)). The automatic give-up rebuild, loop guard, fresh branch slug, rebuild note, new-issue-for-unlinked-PR and recommended-button UI are not upstream.
features.rationale: Directly reduces manager toil on purely technical failures, with a sane loop guard. Port after briefs/holds since businessHold() and parkBrief depend on them; the stuckPrPick button ordering is a cheap UX win on its own.
features.risks: Closes PRs and files issues automatically on GitHub. Classification of 'technical' is regex over stuckWhy strings, so wording changes in swarm.ts silently change behaviour.

features.title: Floor lead: a standing per-floor agent that owns stuck-PR triage with code-enforced limits (no merge, no shell, escalate only with a complete brief)
features.description: New role 'lead' (AgentRole) per floor, extra to the team (highest free desk, not counted in team size, no issues/QA/fixes, floor setting to turn off, default on). Takes stuck-PR triage over from the CEO (stuckStep, at most MAX_TRIAGES). Runs Claude Code with its own office MCP server (server/lead.ts createLeadTools) scoped to its floor: retry QA, send back, rerun checks, close, rebuild, write_brief, escalate; no merge/file/email/chat tools, and Bash/PowerShell/NotebookEdit disallowed (NO_SHELL, same mechanism upstream uses for the CEO). close/rebuild refuse business-held PRs; escalate is refused unless it carries a gap-free decision brief with >=2 options. Separate triage/cleanup models in Settings -> Floor leads; scheduler pass reroutes unhandled stuck PRs. Design doc docs/floor-lead.md; demo-backed swarm tests in floorLead.test.ts.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has CEO-only triage tools (retry_qa, send_back, rerun_checks, close_pull, escalate) in ceo.ts; no 'lead' role, lead.ts or per-floor scoped tool server.
features.rationale: The pattern (a role-specific agent whose authority is defined by an enforced, scoped tool set, plus per-job model routing: strong model for diagnosis, cheap for cleanups) is exactly what a configurable factory needs for reviewer/triage/lead roles. But it rewires triage and adds ~500 lines to swarm.ts with conflicts in clis.ts/demo.ts/swarm.ts against upstream; port the concept into the factory's role/workflow model rather than replaying the commits.
features.risks: One standing paid session per floor (default on). Hardcoded model ids (claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5) in DEFAULT_LEAD_SETTINGS; Claude-only. Changes upstream CEO triage behaviour (CEO loses triage tools). Not yet reconciled with upstream cloud (Box) agents.

features.title: Floor lead board curation with a board-change log and one-tap undo; fixes for non-business waits
features.description: Lead board jobs wake when the ready backlog drops below minReady, when an issue is held after a person closed its PR, when one keeps failing, and every 4 h (skipped if the board fingerprint is unchanged; cheap model). Board tools: close_issue, merge_duplicates, relabel (manager labels protected), reorder_backlog (auto-assign follows it), split_issue, set_dependencies, release_issue; business-held issues protected. server/boardLog.ts records every change with typed undo steps (reopen, unmerge, relabel back, restore order, close split parts, restore deps, re-hold); Decision room lists the week's changes with Undo (POST /api/board/:id/undo); Monday digest lists them. server/waits.ts fallbacks: closed-PR issues back in line after a day, failing issues retried after 6 h, error desks cleared at 9 min before the 10-min alarm. New Backend.reopenIssue with demo fake.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No boardLog.ts, waits.ts, reorder/split/merge-duplicate tools or undo endpoint upstream; upstream holds a closed PR's issues for the manager (closeCleanup.ts toHold) and skips issues after MAX_ISSUE_FAILURES.
features.rationale: 'Act autonomously but log every change with a typed undo' is a strong governance pattern worth generalizing to all agent-initiated board/state changes in the factory. The specific waits fixes (retry after cool-down instead of waiting on the manager) are independently useful. Requires the floor lead; port later as part of a general audit/undo log.
features.risks: Agent closes/relabels/splits real GitHub issues without prior approval (mitigated by undo). Fallback timings are arbitrary constants.

features.title: QA skips draft PRs that only wait on a manager decision (swarm:hold draft, or draft whose issue is needs-input)
features.description: decision.ts waitsOnDecision(): the QA scheduler leaves such a draft queued instead of testing an empty placeholder repeatedly and creating a duplicate 'needs you' card; it is tested once marked ready or the hold comes off. Ordinary drafts are still tested.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream has no needs-input/swarm:hold concept, so the bug cannot occur there yet.
features.rationale: Only meaningful together with merge holds and needs-input briefs; bring it with that stack to avoid wasted QA sessions.
features.risks: None.

features.title: Plain-language decision alerts: push/ntfy/desktop notifications phrased as question, options, recommendation and why, with Open Approvals / Open PR actions
features.description: server/decision.ts readyDecision/stuckPrDecision/stuckPrPick build a Decision (question, options, pick, one-line why, which Approvals button approves) used by notifyNeedsHuman and held-PR alerts; notify.ts gets a link field, a larger body limit for decisions, and ntfy payloads with click-to-Approvals and Open Approvals / Open PR action buttons. Later commits add brief sections to alerts.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream notify.ts ntfyPayload has no actions/link; needs-human alerts are 'PR #N needs you: <why>'.
features.rationale: Good UX for remote approvals, small pure module with tests. Port together with the decision room so alerts deep-link to the approval card; the ntfy actions part is nearly standalone.
features.risks: Recommendation heuristics are regex over stuckWhy strings.

features.title: Stuck-screen watchdog: restart an agent whose terminal hasn't changed for N minutes, give the task to the manager on the second freeze
features.description: server/stuckScreen.ts (pure, tested) + a 5 s screenTick in swarm.ts hashing each busy agent's terminal screen; settings.stuckMinutes (default 15, 0 = off). First freeze on a task: requeue/restart; second: issue marked as failing (auto-assign skips) or PR to needs-human; phone gets one line with the last screen line. Demo: SWARM_DEMO_HANG=stall|mcp.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream server/watchdog.ts (#262) already detects quiet sessions (no output/tool activity for QUIET_MS=20 min, nudge, then requeue) and stuck desk setup; the screen-hash signal and per-task strike rule are new.
features.rationale: Overlaps upstream's watchdog; a second independent timer duplicates logic. If a frozen-dialog case is not caught by upstream's activity signal, fold 'screen unchanged' into watchdog.ts as another problem kind. Conflicts in cliRunner.ts, demo.ts, swarm.ts on cherry-pick.
features.risks: Restarting a long-thinking session wastes tokens if the CLI legitimately stops redrawing. Needs re-check against upstream cloud Box terminals.

features.title: Prevent Claude Code's 'new MCP servers found in this project' dialog from blocking unattended sessions
features.description: clis.ts projectMcpServers() reads the worktree's .mcp.json and cliRunner.ts writes their names into disabledMcpjsonServers in the office's --settings for Claude Code (office's own playwright/office servers excluded), so the CLI never stops at the approval dialog. Fallback: if the dialog appears before the first tool call, the office presses Esc via a new AgentTerminal.press() that does not count as a viewer interrupt, logs it and messages once per floor.
features.already_upstream_evidence: No disabledMcpjsonServers / enableAllProjectMcpServers / .mcp.json handling in upstream server/cliRunner.ts or clis.ts.

features.title: Cost boards: measured token telemetry for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode with priced estimates
features.description: Parses each CLI's own structured session data (Claude transcript/SDK result/status line, Codex rollout token_count events, OpenCode session messages via plugin) into one normalized UsageRecord (uncached/cached/cache-write/output/reasoning tokens). shared/cost.ts holds a dated rate table (Claude, DeepSeek with peak/off-peak tiers), manager overrides, provenance (reported/estimated/free/unavailable), dedupe across resumes, and last-24h tokens/hour and USD/hour by model. Wired into SessionResult, mission control, the manager console and agent cards; docs/costs.md; demo seeds all cost kinds.
features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream cliRunner.ts only takes a Claude costUsd from the status line (line ~627); no token normalization, no Codex/OpenCode cost, no shared/cost.ts or server/telemetry.ts.
features.rfc_relation: cost telemetry, model routing (foundation for per-model cost decisions and budgets)
features.rationale: The only fork work that gives real per-model cost data across all three CLIs, which budgets and routing need. Pure parsers with fixtures and 450 lines of tests. Trial apply conflicts in 7 files incl. cliRunner.ts, which upstream rewrote for cloud boxes, so port the pure shared/cost.ts + server/telemetry.ts first, then rewire.
features.risks: Hard-coded price table goes stale (needs override UI and source dates kept honest); parsers read CLI-internal transcript/rollout formats that drift between CLI versions; subscription usage shown as API-equivalent dollars could mislead.

features.title: QA a PR with a different coding agent (then a different model) than its author

features.already_upstream_evidence: Upstream handOut.ts pickTester(free, author, owed, othersCan, waitedMs) has no pairing parameter; no qaPairing test.
features.rfc_relation: spec/review: independent review by a different model/provider
features.rationale: Small, well-tested and directly implements cross-model independent review. Depends on shared/cli.ts resolveCli from the CEO-CLI commit and upstream's sessionRuntime now also handles box hosts, so re-derive runtimeCli against upstream's current sessionRuntime.
features.risks: None external. Preference only: a single-CLI floor gets no independence.

features.title: Per-floor dollar budgets with 80% warning and 100% hold on new issues

The office accumulates only reported session cost per floor; at 80% it posts an office message and a notification, at 100% startIssueWork stops handing out new issues on that floor (QA and fixes continue) until the cap is raised. Unrounded ratio for levels, re-arming on raised cap, persistence, demo simulate endpoint, HUD/mission console display.

features.rfc_relation: cost telemetry / budgets, approvals (hold until human raises cap)

features.title: CLI-scoped usage pause and automatic Claude-to-Codex failover near Claude's limit

method_notes: Clones: partial clones under scratchpad/forks/<owner>, with upstream main fetched (157efde). Both forks branch from upstream d3b47c6, 8 commits behind. The 8 upstream commits since then rewrote cliRunner.ts and swarm.ts (cloud boxes, local models, --host, preview gateway), so anything touching those files carries more conflict risk. The local git is 2.33, which has no merge-tree --write-tree. Conflict risk was therefore measured by trial `cherry-pick -n` (single commits) and `apply --3way` (branch diffs from their merge-base with fork main) in scratch worktrees at upstream/main (scratchpad/forks-wt/<owner>), reset after each trial. No fork code, npm or tests were run. Squash detection used git patch-id. ceo-configurable-coding-agent = fork main f6abe30. swarm/issue-7-linus = 9faf439. fix/owned-processes-and-reboot = 89f55f5. fix/agent-demo-server-wedge = 7582fb6. swarm/issue-8-linus is contained in fork main. swarm/issue-6-ada is an earlier subset of #11. In konstantinknappe, codex-ceo-codex-cli, codex/ceo-codex-cli-de and 8e1b599 carry the same 47/27-line CEO commit, and deutsch-entwicklung is the integration branch that contains almost everything. No fork feature was found already in upstream main by content or title. Skipped: swarm-qa-evidence in both forks, which is cubefarm's automated QA screenshot branch (EVIDENCE_BRANCH in upstream github.ts), not work. Not verified: CLI behavior claims such as Codex --no-daemon, opencode run vs TUI, and Codex rejecting table-valued -c (upstream already passes -c mcp_servers.playwright={...}, which contradicts iAreEddie's claim), and rate-table correctness. Read only in part: client/UI diffs of cost boards, live playtest, floor managers and the 141-file German sweep. The CEO-CLI, watchdog, quiet-report and dev-server-prompt features are split out of one squash commit (f6abe30), so their line counts are estimates.

features.title: Let the manager pick the CEO's coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode)

The CEO prompt names the tools the way each CLI does (mcp__office__ or office_). features.title: Nano mode: the office as a live view of an external BPMN agent workforce (process floors, step desks, BPMN whiteboards)
features.description: `--nano <url>` replaces the office's own orchestrator with a bridge to nano-workforce and its Camunda-style engine (/v2/process-instances, /v2/jobs, /v2/element-instances). Each running root process instance is a floor, and floor 1 is the bench of idle workers. Desks are the BPMN service tasks of type 'pool:capability', and a worker sits at the desk of the job it holds. Whiteboards draw the instance's BPMN diagram from its DI coordinates, coloured live (held, queued, escalation, human step, waiting, done, ×n rounds). A fleet board sits on the bench. Escalations become phone alerts answered with `answer <id>`, and `start owner/repo#n` hands over an issue. features.title: Remote UI transport: configurable API base and owner token from the URL fragment
features.description: Adds client/src/transport.ts. When VITE_API_BASE is set, every REST call, the /ws and /ws/term sockets, voice clips, screenshots and QA shots go to that origin. Requests carry an owner bearer token, which is taken once from <ui>/#t=<token>, kept in localStorage, and removed from the address bar. WebSocket subprotocols ['bearer', token] carry it there. Images are fetched as blobs. Preview links resolve against the office origin. With VITE_API_BASE empty, behaviour is the same as before. Includes a Vitest test.

The server must validate the token on REST and choose the 'bearer' WebSocket subprotocol (ws handleProtocols). Otherwise browsers reject the WS handshake and the office stays unauthenticated. It also misses client/src/ui/channels.ts and the service worker. Port it together with a server-side token check and a demo-mode fake.

method_notes:
Cloned the 11 assigned forks as blobless partial clones under scratchpad/forks/<owner>, with upstream main fetched (157efde). I ran no code from the forks. Squash merges were detected by content. The local git is 2.33, which lacks `merge-tree --write-tree`, so for each branch I ran `git apply --cached [-R] --check` against a temp index of upstream/main, per file. I also matched commit titles against the upstream log, and matched branch tips against `git ls-remote` refs/pull/*/head. PR and issue states (merged, closed, NOT_PLANNED) came from `gh pr view` / `gh issue view` on leonvanzyl/cubefarm, read-only.

Fully read: every Amdkn diff except pnpm-lock.yaml and part of aspaceHolons.ts; executiveusa; telemoveisvelhos; Paul-Osborn; the faustosip trust-prompt fix; idea-wall shared/ideas.ts and ceo.ts.

Partly read: the large cosmetic faustosip branches (server room, street, makeovers, secrets, personalities, news, cinematic, mods). I judged those from stats, file headers, docs and the upstream QA report on PR #276. I did not read their full diffs.

I did not compare the faustosip branches with the same branches in Calel33/cubefarm: tips 263-285 look identical, but that fork was not assigned to me. Other fork folders in the shared scratchpad (Calel33, iAreEddie, francovp, localloop-pro, konstantinknappe-hash and others) belong to a parallel task, and I did not touch them. francovp's open upstream PR #299 (CEO CLI picker) is relevant to the telemoveisvelhos feature and should be judged by whoever covers francovp.

Not verified: Paul-Osborn's third finding, that a failure to publish evidence does not block a pass. Branches with ahead=0 were skipped.
